# DC_DEFAULTS.md: our own rules where the 2009 client gives no evidence

This file is the project's working ledger: it grew row by row, and the branch names, dates, user decisions and ids in it
record how a rule came about. `specs/README.md` explains the grades and the evidence paths.

The 2009 client never computed these values; the original servers did, and their code is not an allowed source
(`CLEANROOM.md` section 3). Every rule here is **DeCombat policy, written by this project, not Nexon data**. Each is
exposed as a server config key and as a Lua hook (`mod.hooks:wrap`) so operators and mods can replace it. Code
that implements a rule from this file cites it as `// DC-DEFAULT: <id>`.

Allowed inputs for these rules are only things the 2009 client shows or sends: the result screen fields, HUD
timers, kill feed, shop prices from `SHOP_ITEM_LIST.TXT` in the user's ROM, map/mode tables from `GAMEROOM.TXT`,
and the `[MapExp]`/`[MapMoney]` sections of the `.gms` files (ROM data, read at run time).

| id | rule | default | config key | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## B. Corrections of approved rows (evidence column)

- **CD-38**: the evidence "0x347 {1,0} receiver ok" is reversed. The gift window treats `{ok 0, reason 0x20}` as
  "the receiver exists" (`res 0x1808`) and everything else as "no such character" (`res 0x1805`), cs+0x1d55e0. The
  harness (`lobby3`: existing 'Bob' -> {0, 0x20}) agrees. Proposed text: "0x347 {0, 0x20} receiver exists; 0x32b ok".
- **CD-40**: "players waiting" is +0x1e and the client's wait is (+0x16 - +0x12) x +0xe seconds (spec §4.3); the
  queue is per server, FIFO by serial. No change of the rule itself.

- **CD-63 note (disasm-pass):** the client expects a 60/s world update period after the CShell first-run setting (UDP_TRANSPORT addendum). The 10 Hz compatibility default stands until the user's live test; 60 is the candidate value to test first.

confirm or rename when those rows are next edited.

| DSV-21 | Movement relay details: the client's own object is never streamed to it (it owns its body; CD-67 covers the rotation); a remote player whose last accepted update is older than 250 ms (or who is dead) is streamed with velocity 0 so the clients stop extrapolating; rotation is the yaw-only quaternion of the reported view yaw, sent only when it changed for that viewer. The stream's server time (f32 seconds) restarts at 0 when the first client connects to an empty server, so it keeps its resolution on a long-running process (8 ms steps after a day, 31 ms after three days). | 250 ms | the 2009 writer follows a moving record with a velocity-0 record (B §4.2 item 6); `UF_ROT` only on change (B §4.3) | const `STALE_VELOCITY_MS` | `dserver.select_updates` |

Notes for the coordinator:

- DC-C2S-10 is implemented as written (state 3 + 0x88 state 2 before 0x87; spawn set 0xa0 -> 0x6a -> 0xb2 / 0xb3 ->
  0x66 x 4 -> 0x67 state 1; death: state 2 at once, 3 after 2000 ms, respawn 7000 ms after the death).
- DC-C2S-13 is implemented as written (goal in team kills, timer, draw; multi-kill banner from 2 kills within 4 s).
- DC-C2S-7 is implemented with the enable addressed to `pid = 0xFFFFFFFF` (named `TODO_PERF_ENABLE_PID`): the client
  shows its own statistics overlay only when the pid is its own id; whether the reports start without it is UNPROVEN.
- The game layer needs the mode class for the layouts of 0x7d / 0x45 / 0x46 / 0x65; it takes the `room ... type=`
  value the lobby already reads from the ROM mode row (`GameType`), never a hard-coded number.

### hisec-spec

| id | rule (DeCombat policy) | default | 2009 client evidence it must satisfy | config key | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HS-1 | **Drop chance.** In a match of an enabled mode, each kill by a player rolls a HiSec drop with probability p, as long as no case is active in the match and the match has more than `min_players` connected players. Clan matches and bot-only matches never drop. | project decision ("too many hisec cases dropping, should be closer to 1 a game" after the reference stack dropped several in tdm6): DeCombat targets about ONE case per match: p = 1 / expected_kills_per_match (expected kills = the room goal for TDM, else `hisec.expected_kills` 20) per kill, max 1 active case per match, `min_players` 2 for the test phase (4 later), modes = all public modes; enabled by default once the dc-dserver case path exists (HS-2..5) | the case object and 0xd6 messages exist (HISEC §3.1, §3.2); nothing in the client says when 2009 dropped a case (Q-2) | `hisec.enabled`, `hisec.drop_chance`, `hisec.max_active`, `hisec.min_players`, `hisec.modes` | `hisec.should_drop` |
| HS-2 | **Placement.** The case object (create type 0x17, `pickup_kind` 5) appears at the victim's position, with a `case_key` unique within the match (a counter starting at 1), and 0xd6 sub 0 goes to all clients. | victim position; key counter | HISEC §3.1 (kind 5, `case_key` at record +0x48), §3.2 sub 0 (`res 0x18c1` line) | `hisec.place` (`victim` / `killer`) | `hisec.on_drop` |
| HS-3 | **Reservation.** The killer has the case to himself for R seconds: 0xd6 sub 2 {key, killer id} at the drop, then 0xd6 sub 2 {key, -1} when R elapses. R = 0 skips the reserved phase (sub 2 with -1 at once). | R = 10 s | HISEC §3.3: clients hide a case whose owner is someone else; owner -1 = everyone sees it and hears the "timer running out" sound | `hisec.reserve_seconds` | `hisec.reservation` |
| HS-4 | **Despawn timer.** A case not picked up within T seconds of its drop is removed without an award. The server sends the remaining whole seconds to the case object (0xa6, sub 2) once per second while the case exists. | T = 30 s (includes R) | HISEC §3.1 (object sub 2 `remaining`, red at <= 5, Q-1 unit), §3.3 | `hisec.lifetime_seconds` | `hisec.on_expire` |
| HS-5 | **Pickup.** A living player touching the case picks it up (server-side trigger radius), only the owner during the reservation; 0xd6 sub 1 {key, player} to all clients, then the object is removed. Spectators, dead players and players of a finished match cannot pick up. | radius 64 world units | HISEC §3.2 sub 1 (the player must be in every client's roster or the clients do nothing) | `hisec.pickup_radius` | `hisec.can_pickup` |
| HS-6 | **Delivery.** A picked-up case becomes one inbox row of the configured HiSec case product at once (kept even if the player leaves the match); the player gets 0x3014 when he is back in the lobby. One case per row (CD-02). | product = the first ROM product whose item is a HiSec case (HISEC §4.1); operators may name one | inbox rows PROTOCOL_2009 §4.3; HiSec case test HISEC §4.1 | `hisec.case_product` | `hisec.deliver` |
| HS-7 | **Key match and consumption.** Opening a HiSec case (0x32e) needs one owned, unexpired key whose first `FunctionValue` equals the case's and whose `SubType` is 0x13; the server consumes exactly one key count (the oldest-expiring key first) together with the case row, atomically. Without a usable key: 0x32f ok 0, reason 0x99 (a value outside the client's reason table, so the client prints its generic server-error line with the number and keeps the row); the case row stays. | as stated | HISEC §4.2 (client checks locally, the request names no key), §4.3 (+0x1e = key uid, decremented by the client), reason handling cs+0x14e010 | `hisec.key_rule` | `hisec.consume_key` |
| HS-8 | **Award draw and duration.** The award is a uniform pick from the case's ROM pool (as CD-76); the duration is drawn from a HiSec table separate from CD-01: 7 days 50 %, 30 days 35 %, permanent 15 %; extension rules as CD-76. 0x32f uses the case layout with +0x1e = the key's unique id. | `[[7,50],[30,35],[0,15]]` (0 = permanent) | CD-01 excludes HiSec cases; pop-up shows the days (HISEC §4.3) | `economy.hisec_case_odds` | `economy.case_award` |
| HS-9 | **Announcement.** After every successful HiSec opening the lobby sends 0x3013 {+6 = 0, +0x12 opener's character name, +0x34 award item number} to every connected lobby session (including the opener and players inside a match). GP awards (+0x16 != 0) are not announced. | on | HISEC §2 (+6 must be 0; in-match branch exists) | `hisec.announce` (`all` / `channel` / `off`) | `hisec.announce` |
| HS-10 | **Dated substitution.** Optional list of {from, to (UTC timestamps), weekday mask, origin id, replacement id}: while a window is active, a HiSec case drop (HS-6) or an award (HS-8) whose id equals `origin` uses `replacement` instead. | empty | the 2009 host config has `EventHisec<n>` sections with dates, weekday, `OriginID`, `ChangeTo` (HISEC §3.4; target id UNPROVEN, Q-4) | `hisec.events` | `hisec.substitute` |
| HS-11 | **Test trigger.** Lobby chat `!hisec <item number>` broadcasts 0x3013 with the sender's name and that item, without any case or key. Accepted only when the server runs in test mode or the sender is an operator (shell operator flag); otherwise the line is normal chat. | test mode or operator only | HARNESS: lobby_harness::test_lb5cash (expects 0x3013 len 0x38 at `b2`) | `hisec.test_trigger` | none |
| HS-12 | **Reserved: secondary password (future DeCombat client only).** If a later DeCombat client adds a second secret, the server stores only a salted slow hash (Argon2id, m = 19 MiB, t = 2, p = 1, 16-byte random salt per account; PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 600 000 iterations as fallback), compares in constant time, allows 5 wrong attempts per 15 minutes per account, then locks the protected action for 15 minutes; an operator command clears the secret and the lock and is logged. Not used by the 2009 client path. | off (no 2009 wire path) | none: HISEC §5 shows no such feature in the 2009 client | `security.second_secret` | `security.second_secret` |

Notes:

- HS-1..HS-5 need the dedicated server (dc-dserver) to create objects of type 0x17 and send 0xd6 / 0xa6; until
  then `hisec.enabled` stays off and only HS-6..HS-9 and HS-11 apply (lobby side).
- HS-7: reasons 0x8b / 0x8c are NOT suitable (the client deletes the row view and shows `res 0x1891`, meaning
  "inbox item expired and deleted", cs+0x14e010). No reason in the client table (cs+0x393f0,
  PROTOCOL_2009_addendum_shop §9) means "key missing"; 0x99 is our pick of an unmapped value, user decision. A
  2009 client reaches this only when its key view is stale (e.g. the key expired between screens).
- HS-8 numbers are a proposal for play-feel only; the user decides (like CD-01).

### lobby-pipe-fixes

| id | rule (DeCombat policy) | default | evidence / why | config key | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOD-1 | A 2009 client cannot send the mod-set hash (HOSTING_AND_MODS.md §4 item 4: the hash travels in the login of the DeCombat client; the 2009 login frame has no field for it). On a server whose mod-set policy is `modded` (non-empty declared set), a login that carries no mod-set hash is refused at login with the existing "server full / version" style refusal (the same reply the lobby already gives for an unusable server pick or client version), no account state is touched. With `mods.allow_legacy_clients = true` such a client is let in and treated as a vanilla-view-only client: it sees only the vanilla view of the server (the 2009 server-list entry, which is already vanilla-shaped), and the lobby applies no `requires_client` mod to it. A vanilla server is unaffected. A DeCombat client that sends a hash that differs from the server's is refused regardless of this key. | refuse | The 2009 wire entry stays unchanged for the original client (HOSTING_AND_MODS.md §4 item 1, §5 last bullet); a modded server changes rules (rewards, GM tools, items) that a legacy client would silently play under without having the mods' client halves, which is the situation the mod-set hash exists to prevent. Making the legacy path an explicit operator opt-in keeps the safe behaviour as the default. Design choice, no 2009 evidence. | `mods.allow_legacy_clients` (bool, default false; new key in `dc-config` `[mods]`) | none |

"vanilla-view-only" also blocks `requires_client = true` mods from running server-side for that player, or only hides
them (the row above says they are not applied to that client); (c) the key must also be added to the `dc-config`
schema, `doctor` and the key-coverage test of `tests/config_wiring.rs`.

The flight is integrated in steps of at most 16 ms against the level geometry of DSV-34 (dc-sim ray): a hit reflects the velocity about the surface normal and keeps 0.35 of it; the object rests when it is slower than 100 u/s with a solid within 1 unit below it (or on the world box floor); it never leaves the world box. **Object:** a kind-1 model object created on every client in the world with the type-0x13 blob `[0x13][weapon:u8][ammo:u8][1]`, model = the row's `Model` with its `Skin` (else the weapon's `HHModel` / `HHSkin0`), no render style, scale = `ModelScale` (else 1), flag words 0x1201 / 0x0100 / 0x00400020 / 0, a main animation tracker on animation 0, `pos48` with the launch velocity, the thrower's yaw as rotation (`CF_ROT` and `CF_ROT_SNAP`), an empty attachment list, dims (6, 6, 8); no stream entries during the flight; clients that enter the world during a flight do not get it. **Blast at the fuse:** a removal record, then (unreliable, to everyone) the type-0x06 effect with no hit object (0xFFFF), the thrower's character, the throw's weapon and ammunition, `from` = the release origin, `to` = the blast point, normal (0, 1, 0) and the bullet's opaque bytes (CV2-3); then **area damage** to every living, introduced player whose centre is within `AreaDamageRadius` of the blast and not hidden by the level geometry (ray from 1 unit above the blast point): `AreaDamage x (1 - distance / radius)` (linear falloff), damage type `AreaDamageType`, through the DSV-30 damage path (armour first; the kill feed credits the thrower, a self-kill has no killer); **the thrower is always included, team mates only with the room's friendly fire**. Without an ammunition blast row: 100 at the centre, radius 400. Flights end without a blast when the round leaves the running phase. | as stated | tdm2 §3.4 / D9 (create form, removal and blast 2.5 s later; REFERENCE, ACCEPTED by the real client), S2C §8.2 row 0x13 and the blast row, B §3.5; tdm4 §3.1 items 3, 4 (0x74 `zone` = AreaDamageType, `damage` = AreaDamage of the thrown ammunition; REFERENCE); C2S §4.6 (the client sends only the hold and the release) | `GameTuning::projectile` (`ProjectileTuning`: speed, fuse_ms, gravity, bounce, stop_speed, area_damage, area_radius) | none yet (`dc-config [combat]` keys proposed: `projectile_speed`, `projectile_fuse_ms`, `projectile_gravity`, `projectile_bounce`, `blast_damage`, `blast_radius`; dc-config is not this worker's crate) |

### dserver-hits (merged): hit claims were NOT being dropped (bot-human's 128 claims at skill 100: 119 after the round result, 4 trades from a dead shooter; 39 of 43 in-round claims became damage, the rest trades). Per-claim verdicts + counters (`hits:` line, -verbose), bounded rewind for laggy targets (sim: sprinting target at 60 ms each way 45.5 % -> 100 % accepted), trace slack 16 kept with ROM evidence (0 of 5,343 clear shots refused, 34,218 of 34,257 blocked shots refused). REFERENCE_FINDINGS F1 reworded in the spec (the reference stack traces only its effect record, not the damage decision).

| id | rule | default | evidence | config / switch | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSV-42 | **Hit claim verdicts and bounded rewind.** Every `UP_FIRE` that names a hit object gets exactly one verdict: `accepted`, `accepted_rewound`, or a refusal `not_running`, `incomplete`, `shooter_dead`, `clip_empty`, `throw`, `unknown_victim`, `victim_dead`, `friendly`, `bad_geometry`, `origin_far`, `outside_box`, `wall`, `no_damage` (co-op AI hits are judged by the co-op layer and not counted). The counters go to the log as one `hits: N claims, A accepted (R rewound); refused ...` line at every round end and a `session hits: ...` line at the session end; with `-verbose` every refusal is logged. **Rewind:** when the reconstructed hit point (`origin + hit_dist x dir`) lies outside the victim's box grown by the hit tolerance at the victim's latest position, it is tested against the victim's own path of the last `rewind_ms` before the claim arrived: the accepted `UP_PLAYER_UPDATE` positions, joined by straight segments, starting with the position interpolated at the window start; a spawn or a teleport (also a correction teleport) starts a new path, so the box never moves along a path the player did not walk. The first match (newest segment first) is the victim position for the zone test (head fraction); the DSV-34 trace is unchanged (origin to the reported hit point, which lies in the box at that position). No extrapolation beyond the latest position. The track keeps 1000 ms (the largest accepted `rewind_ms`). | `rewind_ms` 200 (0 = off); `-verbose` off | The shooter aims at the stream copy of the victim, which lags the victim's latest update by the transport, the update interval (15 per second, UDP_SESSION_2009_B.md §10.3), the server tick and the client's interpolation (the 2009 stream reader keeps "pending interpolation state", UDP_SESSION_2009_B.md §4.3, PLAUSIBLE); run speed 285 u/s (MOVEMENT_2009.md §2 `RUN_FWD`). SIM (game_sim `moving_target_claims_are_accepted_with_the_rewind`, 200 correct claims each, target walking back and forth at 15 updates/s, tick 30): loopback 100 % / 100 % (no rewind / rewind 200); 60 ms each way + 100 ms interpolation 85.0 % / 100 %; the same at tick 10: 100 % with rewind; extrapolating shooter 100 % / 100 %; sprint 29 u/update with 60 ms each way: 45.5 % / 100 %; 120 ms each way: 39.5 % / 100 %; sprint with 120 ms each way: 70.5 % with rewind (the bound shows). The window is our choice; the reference stack's rule is UNPROVEN (CAPTURE_tdm6_VALIDATION.md §5.3 item 3). | `-combat rewind_ms=<ms>` (0..1000), `GameTuning::rewind_ms`; `-verbose` (`GameTuning::verbose_hits`); `Game::hit_counters()`. dc-config `[combat] rewind_ms` not yet wired (follow-up) | `combat.on_hit` sees only accepted hits (unchanged) |

## Not defaults: findings for other owners (from the rustclient runs)

- **dc-net-engine (transport):** after `C2S_BYE` the 2009 client sends nothing on the link (no ack, no keep-alive) until
  its own bye copies (C-T12); our link sent one ack + empty reliable block 15 ms after `C2S_BYE` (rustclient1
  611.578). A "quiet after bye" mode in `Link` would match. In-world keep-alives (917 in rustclient1, none in the
  real tdm1 session) are NOT a difference of rule: each came 187-1000 ms after our last ack, and the reference stack left 883
  gaps above 200 ms between its reliable blocks in this two-player session (tdm1 had about 31.6 blocks per second).
- **dc-botclient (bot):** with `--respawn-after 0` the fallback path asks on every poll once the armed request went
  out and the player is still dead (about 25 extra 0x89 in the ~50 ms until state 1). Not triggered in these runs (the
  bot never died: dc-client has no weapons); a guard `fallback_ms == 0 => off` would avoid it.

### B. Blast falloff (DSV-39 amendment, PLAUSIBLE)

| id | change | default | evidence | config key | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSV-39 (amend, falloff) | Replace "`AreaDamage x (1 - distance / radius)` (linear falloff)" by: **full `AreaDamage` within `inner x AreaDamageRadius` of the blast point, then linear to 0 at `AreaDamageRadius`**: factor = 1 for d <= r0, (R - d) / (R - r0) for r0 < d < R, 0 beyond (R = the ammunition row's `AreaDamageRadius`, r0 = inner x R; both ROM keys read at run time). inner 0 restores the plain linear falloff. | inner = 0.25 | Fit table below; samples from damage-calibrate.md §2 (tdm4, tdm2, tdm6; one ammunition row in all three). The victim distance uses the update's position candidate (`shell64` trailer vector), which is **UNPROVEN as the position**; the victims moved at 15 Hz, so a sample's distance is uncertain by several units. Three samples cannot separate this curve from others (an exact two-segment fit has its full radius at 0.262 R and its zero at 0.966 R); PLAUSIBLE only. Unit tests: `game::projectile::tests::rom_blast_tdm4_sample_full_damage`, `rom_blast_tdm2_sample`, `rom_blast_tdm6_sample` (ROM-gated, tolerance 0.6), `blast_factor_shape` (synthetic). | `-combat blast_inner=<fraction>` (dc-config `[combat]` does not know the key yet) | `projectile::blast_factor`, `ProjectileTuning::inner_fraction` |

Fit table (R and the full damage are the ROM row's values at run time; the shares below are the captures' health losses
divided by the tdm4 full-damage observation):

| capture | victim distance (UNPROVEN field) | 2009 health loss | share | linear (old) | inner 0.25 then linear (new) | residual new |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tdm4 | 51.9 | 60.0 (full) | 1.000 | 53.1 | 60.0 | 0.0 |
| tdm2 | 153.8 | 53.2 | 0.887 | 39.5 | 52.7 | -0.5 |
| tdm6 | 211.3 | 42.32 | 0.705 | 31.8 | 42.4 | +0.1 |

Least squares over the inner fraction alone gives 0.254 (residuals 0.0 / -0.3 / +0.3); 0.25 was kept as the round
value. A residual of 0.5 damage is 2.8 units of distance on this ramp, well inside the position uncertainty.

Workers' text verbatim:


### Shot cone: dserver-conecheck

Author: dserver-conecheck (server-side shot-direction validation from `specs/WEAPON_FIRE_2009_addendum_cone.md` AC-6).
Evidence: `reports/dserver-conecheck.md`. Ids DSV-102, DSV-103.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSV-102 (new, implemented; project decision pending on `refuse`) | **Shot-direction check.** Every `UP_FIRE` 0x82 pellet's direction is rebuilt the way the 2009 client builds it and compared with the claimed `dir`: the two draws of the cone table at `(stat - 2) mod N` and `(stat - 1) mod N`; the half-width from the weapon row's `MinPerturb` / `MaxPerturb` (the zoomed pair while the zoom bit `moving` is set, the triple-shot pair while `wflag` is set; a non-zero value replaces the plain one), scaled by the message's `shot_scale`, for every spread in `[frac / 255, (frac + 1) / 255)` (all binary32); offsets `(2r - 1) h / 1000` along the `aim` rotation's right / up axes, normalised; the best integer half-width of that interval is taken. Verdicts: `cone_ok` (angle <= `cone_tolerance`), `cone_off` (larger, on a link that has drawn from the table before: one of its pellets matched a rebuilt direction tilted more than 10 x the tolerance from the forward axis), `cone_na` (larger, on a link that never did: DeCombat's bots and dc-client today), `cone_unchecked` (short message). The server's counter per link starts at the 0x7d `own_value` it sent (reset on every 0x7d), expects `+2` per pellet with the table's wrap rule (or no move when the row's gate fails: `lo > hi` or `hi <= 0`, then the forward axis is the expected direction), and then follows the message's `stat` (the client is authoritative on the count; a difference is only counted as `stat skew`). Table: the ROM entry `ATTRIBUTES\RANDOMTABLE.TXT` read at run time; without it the table's generator (CRT `rand()` from state 1 x f32(1/32766), identity checked by SHA-256 AC-1.2). Without a ROM row (or with a key the state needs absent) only the cone's shape is checked (any half-width >= 0; counted as `without row bounds`). Modes: `log` = count every pellet, log each `cone_off` pellet (`client N: cone_off weapon W stat S: E rad from the 2009 cone (h H, row bounds LO..HI, frac F, scale X, zoom Z)`, the first 32 per link, then one "further ... counted, not logged" line), one note line per `cone_na` link, nothing refused; `refuse` = as `log`, and a `cone_off` pellet is refused after the clip mirror (the client spent the round): its hit claim gets the hit verdict `cone_off` (no damage), a throw release creates no object, its shot effect takes the miss form (as DSV-101); `cone_na` is never refused; `off` = no check. Counter line `cone: P pellets, A ok, B off (worst E rad, R refused), C na, D unchecked; U without row bounds; stat skew K; mode M` at every round end and `session cone: ...` at the session end. | `cone_check` log, `cone_tolerance` 2e-5 rad | SPEC `WEAPON_FIRE_2009_addendum_cone.md` AC-1 .. AC-6 (DISASM cshell+0x176cb0, +0x2973a0, +0x2974d0, +0x23bca0); PROVEN-REPLAY through the server's own check (`tests/fire_cone_cap.rs`: tdm1, tdm2, tdm4, tdm6, rust7, the tables loaded as the server loads them: 384 of 384 real-client pellets `cone_ok`, 384 within the ROM row bounds, stat skew 0, first stat = own_value 0 + 2; the bot / dc-client links of tdm6 and rust7 958 pellets all `cone_na`, none `cone_off`; without the ROM 384 / 384 `cone_ok` by shape). Refusing is a DeCombat cheat-protection rule: no 2009 server evidence (no capture of a 2009 server's answer to a forged direction). ### client-audio3d

Source: reports/client-audio3d.md. The user's dc-client round: "the audio seems to only play in one ear
depending on direction" and "gun audio extremely loud". No ROM values are quoted. Builds on CLI-83/84 (client-audio) and

| CLI-200 (proposed) | Stereo law of the voices. A 3D voice (ambient / positional) is panned on the pushed listener's right axis with constant power, `L^2 + R^2 = 2 c^2`; the quiet ear never drops below `floor x c` (a sound at 90 degrees: `0.3 c` and `1.382 c`); inside `near` units of the listener the side share shrinks linearly to the centre (`x * d / near`); behind mirrors the front (no front / back cue, no HRTF, no doppler, no cone), above and below pan to the centre. A 2D (local) voice plays at `c` on both ears; `c = 1/sqrt(2)` (the equal-power centre), so the loudest ear never exceeds the voice gain. The old law (one ear silent at 90 degrees, centre unity) stays available as `PanLaw::HARD`. | floor 0.3, near 48 units, centre 0.7071 | ours where the 2009 evidence ends: the engine hands every voice to the mixer at pan 0.5 (EVIDENCE engine+0xdc190 start, engine+0xdb750 distance law), 3D voices with `min = inner`, `max = outer + 0.01`, rolloff 0.0, listener position and orientation from the camera at 10 Hz and no velocity / cone / 3D-provider / speaker-config call (SPEC AUDIO_2009 §1, §5.1, §5.2, §5.4: PROVEN by the import table); how the third-party mixer turns that into two speaker levels is internal to its DLL (UNPROVEN, not reverse-engineered). ### client-async-load

Author: client-async-load (dc-client model loader threads, dc-render model instances and uploader). Evidence:

| CLI-260 | In the async mode a model (remote body, face, third-person weapon, dropped weapon, own first-person weapon) is read from the ROM, decoded, mesh-built and uploaded on a loader thread. Until it is ready its object is drawn with nothing: a new character has no model and no box (it counts as drawn), a character whose look changed keeps drawing its previous look, the first-person model and a drop are left out. Each distinct upload key (model file, its texture list, its render-style names, the missing-texture colour) is requested once and kept for the session (no eviction); every object draws its own instance of it, so a later character with a cached look appears in the same frame without a request. ### dserver-headzone

Staged by the dserver-headzone worker, branch `dserver-headzone` (report
`reports/dserver-headzone.md`). Status: PROPOSED. No rule of master changes; DSV-130 records why the
node -> zone rule stays as it is, DSV-131 is a proposal for the user (not implemented). Numbering DSV-130 upward as
instructed; check for collisions before folding.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSV-130 | **The reported hit node is an unvalidated hint, resolved through the victim's own skeleton row; an unusable node falls back to the box.** `UP_FIRE`'s `extra_kind` indexes the `[Skeleton<s>]` nodes of the victim's body row (s = its `[Model<n>] Skeleton`). A node that exists gives its `Node<k>DamageFactor` and `Node<k>Location` (DSV-30); a node that does not exist (index beyond the row, or the client's 0xff for none) gives the box rule (DSV-11: head band 2.0 / body 1.0). The server does not check the node against the hit point's height or the node's `Radius`. A level shot at a standing player is a head hit by geometry: the shooter's eye and a standing target's head are both about 33 above the box centre (eye 83.1, box centre 50.1 in the arena), so both the box and the node rule call it a head hit, and the head factor of the ROM (6.0 x InstDamage 35 = 210, health 100) is a one-shot kill. | node from the victim's row, else box | EVIDENCE cshell+0x1e4760 (the client reads `Node<k>Name`, `DamageFactor`, `Parent`, `Location`, `Radius`, `Priority` of every `[Skeleton<s>]` row: the same table); cshell+0x1e14f0 (location accessor; a value above 5 reads as 0); cshell+0x235c00 (the reported node is the nearest node with `Radius` > 0 whose sphere the shot segment crosses, 0xff when none) and cshell+0x235220 -> cshell+0x234fb0 (DISASM: the shot's object filter for a character calls the any-node-sphere test, so a ray that misses every node sphere does not register on the character at all); PROVEN-CAPTURE: the 2009 client reported node 53 for a head hit 33.3 above the victim's centre (CAPTURE_tdm6 2.1); OBSERVED (arena 20261026_033350 / _032858): the reference stack reported node 53 at 33.0 and node 9 at 33.8 above the centre on level shots at a standing bot, one-shot kill, `hit_zone` 1; ROM: node 9 and node 53 of `[Skeleton0]` are face nodes (head location, factor 6.0) | none | none |
| DSV-131 (proposal, NOT implemented) | **Optional node plausibility check.** With `combat.node_check = band` the server treats a claimed node whose location is head (1) as a head claim only when the hit point lies in the head band of the box (DSV-11 `head_fraction`) and a node with `Radius` 0 as no node; else the box rule applies. Off by default: the 2009 claim data (head 33.3, shoulders 24-27, chest 15.1 above the centre) leave only a 6-unit gap between the head and the shoulder bands, and the node's world position needs the animated pose the server does not have. | off | cshell+0x235c00 (only nodes with `Radius` > 0 are ever reported); captured claim heights as in DSV-130 | `combat.node_check` (proposed) | none |

Per shot: the drain up to the shot, then the pitch kick of CLI-64 (with the TripleShotMax / TripleShotBase pair in triple-shot mode when both are set), then `back := max(back, 0) + BaseCamBackJitter`, then, when `a > MaxRandomPitch` (raw row value compared with radians), the **yaw kick**: `f = rad(BaseCamRecoilWagL or ...WagR by the side) x (1 - \|w\| / rad(MaxCamRecoilWag))`, `w += f / 2`, view yaw `-= f`; the side flips when `\|w\| > MaxRandomWag` (raw, radians) and the millisecond tick clock reads an odd value (the 2009 `GetTickCount() & 1`; ours: the session tick clock of CLI-61). ## Proposed rows from bot-loadflakes (PENDING user approval, 2026-10-26; on stage, master merge after the playtest)


bot-loadflakes: dc-botclient join timeout option (default stays the 2009 10 s) and a dserver slow-pass log line (>= 1 s main-loop pass, phase split); shooter_loopback rewritten onto events (10/10 alone; the loaded proof is still to run). Workers' text verbatim:


### bot-loadflakes

| id | rule | status |
|---|---|---|
| BOT-50 (new; renumber at fold if taken) | dc-botclient / dc-net-engine: the time a joining bot repeats its `OOB_JOIN_ASK` (every 300 ms, UDP_TRANSPORT_2009.md §5.2) before the start fails with 0x4F is configurable. `Joiner::with_timeout(ms)`, `GameConfig::join_timeout_ms`, `BotConfig::join_timeout`, CLI `--join-timeout <s>` (clamped 1..3600 s). The default stays the 2009 client's 10000 ms (`JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS`), so `dc-client` and every existing bot run behave as before. A test or load tool whose game server runs on a machine at full CPU load passes a longer limit (the loopback tests use 120 s); a server that really is gone still fails, after that limit. No wire change. | proposed, TESTED (dc-net-engine `a_longer_limit_keeps_asking`; `shooter_loopback` uses 120 s, alone 10/10; loaded rounds pending) |
| DSV-135 (new; renumber at fold if taken) | dc-dserver main loop: when one pass of the loop (pass start to next pass start) takes 1000 ms or longer, the server logs `slow pass: N ms since the previous one (control lines a ms, datagrams b ms, timers and output c ms; ...)`. A log line only (stdout and `-log`); no behaviour change, no wire change. The server is one thread: a pass that long delays every client's join reply and acknowledgements, and the phase split tells a blocked server (a phase holds the time) from a descheduled process (the phases are short, the gap is outside them). | proposed, built; no unit test (a pass cannot be slowed from outside on a controlled schedule); to be observed in load runs |

## Proposed rows from bot-loadflakes-2 (PENDING user approval, 2026-10-26; on stage)


bot-loadflakes-2: the loaded shooter_loopback failures were LOST UDP DATAGRAMS: a Windows receive timeout on a UDP socket drops datagrams that arrive as the timeout expires, wider under CPU load (Python two-socket test: 9 of 60 lost with the timeout, 0 with select); dc-dserver's runner and the bots read with a 2 ms timeout. New SocketReader in dc-net-engine (a thread blocks in recv with no timeout and feeds a channel; the loops wait on the channel). No wire change. Workers' text verbatim:


### bot-loadflakes-2

| id | rule | status |
|---|---|---|
| BOT-51 (new; renumber at fold if taken) | dc-botclient `run_game*`: the game UDP socket is read by a thread that blocks without a receive timeout (`dc_net_engine::socket_reader::SocketReader`); the loop waits for a datagram on a channel with the old 2 ms poll wait. The socket no longer has `SO_RCVTIMEO`. Reason: on Windows a receive timeout loses datagrams under CPU load (measured, see bot-loadflakes-2.md: a bot needed 5 to 12 join asks or never joined within 3 s in 3 of 12 loaded rounds; 0 of 32 after). No wire or protocol change. The run also logs an `udp_io` event (datagrams in / out, connection-reset notices, errors). | proposed, TESTED (`socket_reader` unit tests; shooter_loopback 6/6 and 8/8 under 32 and 100 hogs) |
| DSV-136 (new; renumber at fold if taken) | dc-dserver main loop: same receive thread for the server socket (the server's asks and acknowledgements were lost the same way). A failed send is logged (first 5, with the peer) and at the end of the run the `-log` file (not stdout: `@end` stays the last stdout line) gets `udp host: <HostStats>` and, per peer, datagrams received / sent / failed sends. | proposed, TESTED (e2e_loopback, rom_world, game_sim, shooter_loopback) |

### client-fps (Wave AN)

Author: client-fps (user retest finding 14: the windowed client feels slower than the 2009 client; the exit FPS line
was missing when the window closed from the room screen). Evidence: `reports/client-fps.md`.
These are client-side rules and engineering only. No server rule value is involved. Ids are REN-60 upward and CLI-390 upward.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REN-60 | Per-object sun cache for model lighting. Each model object keeps the position of its last sun test and that test's result. The test runs again only in two cases: the object has no result yet, or it has moved more than `model_sun_variance` + 0.001 from the kept position (squared distance; the variable is at its 2009 default of 0.05). Otherwise the kept result is used. Ours: (1) every model object the client draws is treated as one that has the 2009 move flag set (bit 0x10 of object +0x88): characters and corpses by object id, dropped weapons by object id, and the own first-person weapon. Which objects the 2009 engine marks with the flag is not traced. (2) A key's entry lives as long as the world, and object ids are 16-bit. (3) The first light set of an object equals `WorldLights::light_set` at the same position. Later sets differ only while the object stays within 0.051 units of its last test. | on | EVIDENCE engine+0x1b21b0; DISASM engine+0x1b243b..0x1b24c8 (result at +0x7750: below 0 means none yet; flag test; position kept at +0x7744..+0x774c; refresh); DISASM engine+0x1b2451..0x1b2472 (variance at VA 0x6d443c, initialised to 0.05, plus the constant 0.001 at VA 0x6731a0); EVIDENCE engine+0x135e0 (squared-distance test) | none | `world::WorldLights::light_set_for`, `world::SunObject`, `characters::light_set_for` |
| REN-61 | Pruned point ray for the sun test (engineering, no rule of its own). The sun test traces the world diagonal from the object toward the sun. 2009 does the same (DISASM engine+0x1b1cc0..0x1b1d44: offset = -(extents diagonal) x sun direction). The test now uses `CollisionWorld::ray_pruned`. Each BSP node carries the part of the segment that lies inside it (each plane widened by 0.01 units), cut at the nearest hit so far. A node whose part lies on one side of its plane descends that side only, and a child with an empty part is skipped. The faces still tested are tested in the sweep's order, with the sweep's test and its 0.1 back-off between models. A world with blocker polygons falls back to `ray`. | on | DISASM engine+0x1b1cc0 (ray length = world extents diagonal); tests: dc-sim `pruned_rays_equal_the_sweep_in_random_box_worlds` (36,000 rays, 12 random box worlds, including grid-snapped worlds with shared planes) and `rom_pruned_rays_equal_the_sweep_on_every_world` (42,000 rays on all 21 ROM worlds, `Hit` equal field by field; 3.9 s for the sweep vs 0.12 s pruned) | none | `dc_sim::CollisionWorld::ray_pruned`, `world::WorldLights::sun_visibility` |
| CLI-390 | Exit report on every path. Every way a game window ends prints the exit report: the window mode's own run, and every match the menu starts (the menu path dropped it before, so a window closed from the room screen after a match showed no FPS line). | CLI-391 | Radar map layer. (a) The layer is composed with the per-pixel arithmetic of the bilinear wrap sampler, but each column's and each row's texel indices and fraction are worked out once, not with four 64-bit remainders per pixel. The pixels are identical (test against the per-pixel reference, for windows inside the picture, across its edges and far outside). (b) In the windowed client only, the layer is composed on a thread of its own while the player moves. The frame keeps drawing the last composed layer until the new one is back, so the picture under the disc follows a player position at most one composition (a few ms) old. ### w1-bgm (Parity Wave 1)

Branch `w1-bgm` (task W1-2 background music). ROM keys are given as sha256(name)[:16] / length.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |

| AUDIO-1 (proposed) | **Bounded music path.** BGM files are decoded on one worker thread (never the frame thread). Request slot: 1 (latest cue wins; a cue replaced before it starts decoding never decodes). Result slot: 1 (a result of a replaced cue is dropped). File size over 8 MiB is refused (no music, one log line); the ROM's largest music file is 3.4 MB. Decoded audio longer than 24 Mi f32 samples (96 MB) is cut at that length. Two decoded tracks stay resident (the playing one and the one before it, so front end <-> waiting room <-> loading re-cues cost no decode). Music log: 64 lines. One monotonic music clock (process start) drives play, fade and update for menu and match, so the 1 s fade never sees the game clock restart; in a match frame the effects update (game clock) runs with the music player taken out of the mixer, so only the music clock steps a fade. Decoded audio is cut at 96 MB for what stays resident; the decode peak is bounded by the 8 MiB file cap (the whole file is decoded before the cut). | on | docs/RENDER_PERF_GATES.md (bounded budgets, deterministic degradation); tests `latest_cue_wins_and_stale_result_is_dropped`, `match_frames_keep_the_music_fade_on_the_music_clock`, `missing_files_and_oversize_are_refused`, `log_is_bounded`; ROM: 4 distinct tracks decode to 12.6 M, 12.6 M, 8.8 M, 2.4 M and 0.18 M samples (all under the cap) | constants in `dc-client/src/music.rs` | `SoundDirector::music_cue`, `music_tick` |

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |

| SIM-18 (amends SIM-3, implemented) | **Doors and switches are solid world models.** The collision set takes the models linked to objects of the mover classes (sliding door, rotating door, rotating switch; class keys by hash) like the plain-world-model and breakable roles. CLI-230 still decides per frame: solid only while the server's named brush of that name has 0x2000. Offline (no server, CLI-233) they are solid at the file position. | on (`WorldFilter::movers` = the three class keys) | PROVEN: MOVEMENT_2009 §9.6 stage 2 (engine+0x78280: world-model objects that pass the solid flag rules take the BSP sweep); DSV-46 (the reference stack created the tdm4 sliding doors with flag word 0x3101, which holds the 0x2000 solid bit; REFERENCE, accepted). OBSERVED (survey 2026-10-26): 23 sliding doors, 42 rotating doors, 2 rotating switches in the ROM worlds, all linked to a model and all with the solid property set | `WorldFilter::movers` (empty = the former rule) | `dc-sim from_world::{MOVER_CLASSES, WorldFilter::is_mover, selected_models}` |
| CLI-420 (amends CLI-251, implemented) | **A mover is drawn and solid where its server object is.** Every point `p` of the file model is placed at `pos + rot * (p - origin)`: `origin` = the model origin of the file, `pos` / `rot` = the object's latest decoded position and rotation (identity without a rotation). ### fix-hang (client hang fixes)

Branch `fix-hang`. Ids CLI-460, CLI-461. Report `reports/fix-hang.md`.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-460 | A lost GPU device (driver reset / TDR) never hangs the client. wgpu-core 25.0.2 deadlocks the thread that meets a lost device inside `Queue::submit` or `Device::poll` (it holds the device's snatch lock for reading and `lose()` takes it for writing). The device-lost callback that `lose()` runs first unwinds that thread instead; the window catches it around its frame (and around the resize reconfigure), hides itself, leaks the lost device's GPU objects (dropping them can meet the same deadlock) and leaves the match with exit reason `gpu device lost`: the menu path returns to the waiting room (new window, new device), a direct join ends the run. If the frame does not come back within the watchdog's phase budget the process exits with code 3 instead of hanging, after a stall dir without minidump and the profiler's flight recorder (amended by CLI-GATE-T1-1: exit 3 = the frame did NOT recover, a failed run for the hang gate; only the window leaving the match by itself, exit 0, is a recovery). The menu window reopens after a device loss at most 3 times per process; the 4th loss ends the menu with an error and a clear message. A known device loss exits before any minidump is attempted. AMENDED by gpu-recover: the window first REBUILDS the GPU side inside the match (new instance, surface, adapter, device, queue; every renderer; the world's render scene loaded again from the ROM with the server's world-model and sky state applied again; model and effect uploads again from the CPU caches, drawn with nothing until back; the lost device's objects retired, never dropped; the old surface dropped first); the simulation and the network go on, nothing is drawn meanwhile, watchdog phase `recovering` (15 s budget); it prints `GPU device recovered in N ms` and plays on. Attempts every 250 ms; after 12 s without a device it leaves the match as above. `DC_GPU_RECOVER=0` = leave at once. Test knob `DC_FAULT=gpu_lost` + `DC_FAULT_AT` (DC_AGENT=1 / debug) = the loss path without a driver reset. | on | fix-hang report: the user's two hangs and soak 1 = this deadlock after `nvlddmkm` 153 driver resets; `tests/gpu_loss.rs` (manual, a real TDR): returns in 3.6 s with the callback, deadlocks (90 s time-out) without it; window proof run `20261026_233516_fixhang_lossproof` (`DC_GPU_LOSS_TEST_AT=40`: window left the match, menu back in the room) | `DC_GPU_LOSS_TEST_AT=<s>` (test: provoke a real reset) | `gpulost::{watch, guard, provoke}`, `window::App::on_gpu_reset`, `watchdog::report` |
| CLI-461 | Frame watchdog in the window: a thread notes the frame counter every 500 ms; after 3 s without a frame it writes `dc-client.hang.txt` (last finished profiler stage, the last 32 frame events, the stacks of every thread: each suspended only while its registers and stack are copied, walked with dbghelp, symbolized from the PDB next to the exe) and `dc-client.hang.dmp` (MiniDumpWithThreadInfo + IndirectlyReferencedMemory) next to the sound log, once per process. Cost: one relaxed atomic add per frame, one store per profiler lap. SUPERSEDED in its stall rule and report layout by CLI-GATE-T1-1 (phase budgets, stall dirs, second dump + abort); `dc-client.hang.txt` stays as a copy of the first stall dir's threads.txt. | on (window) | fix-hang report (it found the deadlock in soak 1); tests `watchdog::tests::*`, `dc-hangdump::tests::a_spinning_thread_is_sampled_with_a_symbolized_stack` | `DC_WATCHDOG=0` off, `DC_WATCHDOG_DIR=<dir>`, `DC_WATCHDOG_SELFTEST=<s>` (a 4.5 s stall for the proof) | `watchdog::{arm, frame, stage, event}`, crate `dc-hangdump` |

### gate-hang (gate T1)

Branch `gate-hang`. Ids CLI-GATE-T1-1, CLI-GATE-T1-2 (staging names, not yet renumbered). Report `reports/gate-hang.md`.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-GATE-T1-1 | The client's hang watchdog (supersedes CLI-461's stall rule). Progress = frames + event-loop passes + phase changes; phase budgets: menu / play / headless 2 s, loading 15 s, teardown 10 s, idle unwatched (the wait for the match server has its own time-out); a poll more than 2 s late (machine suspended) restarts the clock. A stall over budget writes `stall_<pid>_<n>/` (`stall.json`: kind, pid, frame thread, phase, budget, stalled ms, frame, stage, the threads inside a wait from the breadcrumbs; `threads.txt`: breadcrumbs per thread, the last 32 frame events, every stack; `events_tail.jsonl`: last 64 `--events` lines; `dump1.dmp`), at most 3 dirs per process; at budget + 6 s `threads2.txt` + `dump2.dmp`, then abort (exit 0xC0000409). A lost GPU device whose frame did not come back (CLI-460): a stall dir with kind `gpu_lost_no_recovery` and NO minidump, the profiler flight recorder (DC_PROF_TAIL) flushed, exit code 3. A panic (not the GPU-loss unwinding, not after a device loss) writes `panic_<pid>.txt` (message, place, thread, breadcrumbs, backtrace); an unhandled SEH exception writes `crash_<pid>/crash.dmp` (+ exception record) and `crash.txt` (the folder and an empty dump file are made at start-up and removed at a normal end). Report folder: `DC_WATCHDOG_DIR`, else the `--sound-log` folder, else the `--heartbeat` folder, else the working directory `.`. Exit codes: 0 normal / recovered GPU loss, 3 GPU loss without recovery, 0xC0000409 watchdog abort. Breadcrumbs: a per-thread lock-free ring (64 threads x 16 crumbs), allocation-free on every crumb. | on (windows); headless only with `DC_WATCHDOG=1` | Our own diagnostics (no 2009 behaviour). Gate T1 soaks: the deployed a579a3f hung on a natural driver reset pair and was caught by the external watchdog; the gate-hang build recovered from two; `DC_FAULT=deadlock_test` stall dirs name both threads | `DC_WATCHDOG=0` (no watchdog thread), `DC_WATCHDOG=1` (headless), `DC_WATCHDOG_ABORT=0` (no abort), `DC_WATCHDOG_DIR`, `DC_CRUMBS=0`, `DC_FAULT=deadlock_test` + `DC_FAULT_AT=<s>` (default 5; only with `DC_AGENT=1` or a debug build) | `watchdog::{arm, frame, pump, phase, install_crash_reports}`, `dc_hangdump::{crumb, crash, process}` |

### fix-musicloop (music and live lines)

Branch `fix-musicloop`. Id AUDIO-3 (proposed).

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |

| AUDIO-3 (proposed) | **Music and live lines in the sound log.** Every music cue (`cue`), server order (`order`, S2C 0xd9), track start (`play`, with its length) and stop (`stop`) is one `trigger: "music"` line of the sound log (fields `op`, `cue`, `phase` menu/match, `loop`, `fade_s`, `dur_ms`, `music_file_hash`, `music` = the player's state; `file_hash` is null so start-only readers skip it). ### perf-hitch (frame hitches)

Branch `perf-hitch`. Ids CLI-440, CLI-441. Report `reports/perf-hitch.md`.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-440 | Sound files and footstep rigs are prepared off the frame thread. (a) Decoded sound files live in a cache of at most 128 MB of samples. When a new file would pass the cap, the least recently used files that no voice is playing are evicted. A file that still does not fit plays but is not cached (counted). (b) In async mode a decode thread fills the cache ahead of use: the footstep, jump and hit-feedback files of the ROM tables when the director opens, every WAV of a server preload list (it was decoded inside one frame before), and the whole sound set of a weapon once any of its sounds plays. At most 1024 names wait and 8 are in flight; a further name is dropped and counted. A sound that is not cached yet is still decoded inline when it plays, so every sound plays the same samples, at the same time, as before. (c) In async mode the footstep keys of a body model are read on a rig thread (at most 4 models wait; a further one is asked for again on a later frame). The body has no footsteps until they arrive: about 130 ms after it is first seen on this machine. Async mode is on in the window and off in headless runs and tests, with the same switch as the model loads (CLI-262). | window async, headless inline | perf-hitch report (frame 0 of the network run 160 ms to 26 ms; the sound stage of frame 0 147 ms to 11 ms; rig read 131 ms measured); tests `sndcache::tests::*`, `sound::tests::rom_async_rig_arrives_equal_to_the_inline_read` | `DC_ASYNC_LOADS=1` / `0` | `sndcache::PcmCache`, `SoundDirector::set_async_decode`, `SoundDirector::rig` |
| CLI-441 | Session logs (the sound log, the capture and the JSONL event log of the client and the bots) are written by one writer thread per file through a queue of at most 8192 lines and 4 MiB. The thread that records a line never touches the file. Before, one blocking write per sound start ran on the frame thread, and the event log was flushed after every line while the network thread held the session lock. A full queue drops the newest line and counts it (a capture shows the gap in `seq`). The writer flushes whenever its queue runs empty. The exit report prints lines written and dropped, the queue high-water marks and the longest single write. File formats are unchanged. | on | perf-hitch report: with an injected 150 ms write stall every 2 s (`DC_LOG_STALL=2000:150`), 19 frames over 50 ms before and 0 after | `DC_LOG_STALL` (fault injection for measurements only) | `dc_botclient::logring::LogWriter`, `record::Recorder`, `SoundDirector::log_to` |

### bot-los (bots stop staring at enemies through walls)

Branch `bot-los`. Ids BOT-52, BOT-53 (renumber at fold if taken). DeCombat bot behaviour; no 2009 evidence applies (our own bot).

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BOT-52 (new, proposed) | **The way-finder notices when it is stuck and follows the obstacle.** At each decision (BOT-17) the hunter is stuck when the body moved under 24 units in the last 1 s, or when its flat distance to the goal did not drop by 64 units in 3 s (sliding to and fro along a wall the goal lies behind). A stuck hunter flips its side (+/-) and sidesteps: it follows the obstacle on that side (headings scanned from a quarter turn toward the side, turning away from it; the first whose 0.5 s probe moves 70 % of the freest probe) until it is 64 units closer to the goal than where it got stuck, at most 8 s; the stall check pauses meanwhile. Outside a sidestep each heading's score also gets 0.5 per unit its probe falls short of the freest probe (along a wall beats into it). `hunt_stuck` now counts these sidesteps. | as stated | playtest report ("bots run at the wall"); unit `a_hunter_in_a_cup_backs_out_and_finds_the_goal` (old finder: no line of sight in 20 s, slides along the back wall at 1216 units from the goal; new: line of sight at 14.2 s), `no_progress_for_a_second_starts_a_sidestep` | none (constants in `hunt.rs`) | `hunt::Hunter::steer` |
| BOT-53 (new, proposed) | **An enemy behind world collision is unseen ("occluded").** The line from the bot's eye (`EYE_FRACTION`) to the enemy's aim point (BOT-12) is swept against the loaded world (`hunt::line_clear`); a blocked enemy gets `unseen_reason` "occluded" (event `target_unseen`), is never chosen, aimed at or shot at; the nearest visible enemy is chosen instead. With no enemy in sight the hunt goal is the nearest occluded enemy's current position (before VIS-13's last-seen patrol); an occluded enemy's streamed position also counts as its last known position for that patrol (else an enemy the server culls before it was ever in sight leaves no goal: live 3-bot round on JUNK_FLEA, 0 kills in 180 s); once the line clears it is a target again (`target_seen`) and normal aiming resumes. No world loaded: nothing is occluded (as before). | on | playtest report ("stuck looking at the enemy through the wall"); units `an_occluded_enemy_is_not_aimed_at_and_becomes_the_goal`, `a_visible_enemy_wins_over_a_nearer_one_behind_the_wall` (both fail on 556eda3: the nearer enemy behind the wall was chosen) | none | `shooter::sight_reason`, `Shooter::choose` |

| BOT-59 (new, proposed; taken as next free 54 + 5 because the bot-los branch was told to take BOT-54) | **Pause / resume switch for play sessions.** The bot polls the file named by env `DC_BOT_CONTROL` once a second (no variable: no polling). Lines `pause` / `resume` (every bot) and `pause <name>` / `resume <name>` (one bot, case-insensitive); the last applicable line wins; no file, an unreadable file or no applicable line = resume. Alt+Enter (CLI-220's key rule) switches the one window between them in the menu and in the match, on the monitor it is on (the primary without one), and the switch is saved to the profile. ## Proposed rows from server-rom (PENDING user approval, 2026-10-29)

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DSV-370 (proposed) | **What a server ROM holds.** `dc-server-rom <client folder> <out folder>` writes every archive's full entry list (names, sizes, archive order) and, as plain files: every text table (`.txt`, `.gms`, `.bms`, decrypted), every entry of `WORLDS.rez`, every effect list (`.fxf`), every model file (`.ltb`) of `CHARS_M_BODY.rez` and `GUNS_M_HH.rez` (body models; third-person weapon models, the dropped weapon's model and animations) and of the eleven first-person weapon model archives `GUNS_M_PV_AR.rez` .. `GUNS_M_PV_Throwing.rez` (the bot's fire cycle, BOT-82; added 2026-10-29 remote-lobby: 916.4 MB, 2828 files); every wave file (`.wav`) only up to and including its `data` chunk header (the game server reads only the play time); the strings image of `Game/CShell.dll` (DOS header, stub, signature and file header, then the printable runs that end in a NUL, no section bytes); the archive key in the manifest. No executable, texture, other model, sound or interface file. ## Remote players under WAN jitter (remote-jitter, 2026-10-29)

Branch `remote-jitter` (wb). Ids CLI-1330 .. CLI-1331. User report 2026-10-29: a friend on a WAN link saw every remote player "lagging / glitchy" while the host on loopback saw nothing. How the 2009 engine smooths remote objects is UNREAD (CLI-11): both rows are OUR rules. Bench `dc-client net::jitter_sim` (30 Hz stream, 60 ms one way): RMS drawn-speed error 40 % -> 2 % at 30 ms jitter, 41 % -> 3 % at 2 % loss + 30 ms, 67 % -> 11 % at 5 % loss + 60 ms; 0 % frozen frames after (0.2 / 0.7 / 4.2 % before). NOT verified on a real WAN link yet.

| Id | Rule | Value | Evidence / reason | Config | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-1330 (new; amends CLI-11) | **Playout clock and jitter-sized delay of remote players.** A stream sample is stamped with the server time of its message (the time entry, B §9.1) mapped to the local clock by the smallest arrival-minus-server offset of the player's last 256 samples (AMENDED 2026-10-31, before 64: the short window's minimum changed every time its fastest sample left, and each change bent one segment's drawn speed, a periodic hitch; without a time entry: on arrival, as before); the map follows a change of that minimum, down or up, at most 10 % of the arrival time passed (a drop never crowds stamps together, a rise never stretches one segment by the whole rise; AMENDED 2026-10-31, before a rise was taken at once; while the map lags a real latency rise the stamps run early, the waits grow and the delay covers it); a sample whose server time is older than the newest one's (a late message) is dropped and counted stale, one less than 2 ms later is dropped uncounted; after 8 of these in a row the track stamps on arrival and tries the server clock again after 3 s once its time advances by 2 ms or more. A stream entry is stamped with the time entry of the message that carried it (`ClientObject::stream_time`). A snap and the first stream sample after it do not seed the stream interval (steps under 1 ms are no interval; the default 100 ms stands until a real one is seen). The delay is max(CLI-11's 1.5 x interval, two intervals + 4 ms (AMENDED 2026-10-31: one lost update never runs the buffer dry, the Source engine's default interp ratio of 2; 70 ms at 30 Hz, 204 at 10 Hz), the longest wait of the last 256 samples + 4 ms, a wait being arrival minus the previous sample's stamp, i.e. the server step plus the arrival lateness, so a lost or skipped update's doubled step counts; a wait above 250 ms is a silence, ignored, and a snap forgets the waits; AMENDED 2026-10-31, before: interval + the 95th percentile of the arrival lateness of the 64 clock-map samples), within CLI-11's 50..250 ms; a stamp step above 250 ms (death, culling) does not enter CLI-11's interval average either; the drawn delay follows that value at most 10 % (rising) / 2 % (falling) of real time, so a change never jumps the body. On loopback the lateness is ~0 and the two-interval floor wins (70 ms at 30 Hz, 204 ms at 10 Hz; before 2026-10-31: 50 / 150). | 256 clock-map samples, slew 10 % both ways; floor 2 intervals + 4 ms; 256 waits, the longest; 250 ms silence bound; 4 ms, 10 % / 2 % | arrival stamps bent the drawn speed by the arrival jitter (bench: 40 % RMS speed error at 30 ms jitter, 2.8 % of frames jumping > 2x the step); 1.5 x 33 ms = 50 ms leaves 17 ms for jitter; 2026-10-31 Mac over Wi-Fi to the Chicago VPS at 30 Hz: q95 4..19 ms yet 3..7 % of the frames late (30..100 late runs per minute per player, 0 on loopback), the spikes beyond q95 came back every 1..4 s and the 64-sample (2 s) window forgot them; the 256-sample maximum keeps the delay up across them; the second Mac match the same day (delay 72..75 ms, no arrival later than 35 ms) still drew Bot1 late 84..120 times a minute, 5..8 % of the frames, a doubled runner at 120 Hz: a tenth of its updates never arrived (266 samples per 10 s at 30 Hz) and the rule covered the mean 35 ms interval, not the 66 ms step; the longest wait covers both; third match: 0 late frames at a 130 ms delay yet a rubber-band feel, so the remaining speed wobble sources were removed: the 64-sample clock-map minimum (changes every ~2 s on a jittery link, each a 20..30 ms stretch of one 33 ms segment) and rises taken at once; the two-interval floor follows the Source engine (cl_interp_ratio 2, 100 ms at 20 Hz) and Gambetta's entity interpolation (one interval behind at least), see docs/NET_LATENCY.md | none (consts `LATE_WINDOW`, `LATE_STAT_WINDOW`, `WAIT_SILENCE_MS`, `LATE_MARGIN_MS`, `DELAY_RISE`, `DELAY_FALL`) | `net::Track::{follow_object_at, push_stream, delay_ms, playout_delay}` |
| CLI-1331 (new) | **Late samples and link statistics.** Past its newest sample a remote player is carried along the newest stream velocity (B §4.3) for at most 100 ms, then eased back to the newest sample over 100 ms (not parked ahead of it); a velocity of 0 (DSV-21's stale record), a speed above 2000 u/s or a snap placement (VIS-13 / CLI-620) carries nothing. Diagnostics: dc-client's event log (`--net-log`) gets one `remote_interp` line per remote player every 10 s, the first window starting when the first remote body appears (samples, stale, stream_gap_ms, late_max_ms (jitter_q95_ms before 2026-10-31), delay_ms, delay_mean_ms, frames, late_frames, held_frames, late_per_min, holds_per_min, server_clock; AMENDED 2026-10-31: moving_frames, speed_mean, speed_cv (spread of the drawn speed over its mean, frames above 30 u/s), backsteps_per_min (a drawn step reversing the previous: a rubber band), jumps_per_min (a step over 3 x the window's mean step)); dc-dserver logs per client every 10 s `client N: link 10 s: rtt, input rate (RFC 3550-form jitter of the 0x64 arrivals against their client time, longest gap), resends, flow drops, datagrams in / out` and `client N: link summary ...` when the link closes. | 100 ms, 2000 u/s, 10 s | a lost or late stream message froze a running player for one or more ticks and then jumped it (bench: 0.7 % frozen frames at 2 % loss) | none (consts `EXTRAP_MAX_MS`, `EXTRAP_MAX_SPEED`, `INTERP_REPORT_MS`, `linkwatch::REPORT_MS`) | `net::Track::{draw, take_report}`, `net` thread loop, `dc_dserver::linkwatch::LinkWatch` |

## TLS on the auth and web ports (tls-auth, 2026-10-30)

Branch `tls-auth` (wc). Ids LG-220 .. LG-226, CLI-1470 .. CLI-1475. All of them are our own deviation from 2009: the
2009 auth protocol carries the login password in clear text on the auth port and the 2009 client has no TLS at all.
User direction 2026-10-30: modern sign-up practice, no password sent unencrypted.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LG-220 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **What is encrypted.** The auth port (login password, nickname creation, server pick) and the web port (registration form, clan pages, mod downloads) speak TLS 1.3 (rustls, `ring` provider). The lobby port and the clan port carry no password and stay plain; the game's UDP traffic is unchanged. Passwords are stored as Argon2id hashes (LG-140). | as stated | none (ours) | none | `tls`, `net::spawn_listener_tls`, `clanweb::spawn_with_tls` |
| LG-221 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **The certificate.** The lobby keeps one certificate and key in its TLS folder (`--tls-dir`, default the DB's folder): `fullchain.pem` + `privkey.pem` when both exist (a CA-issued pair, e.g. Let's Encrypt), else `tls_cert.pem` + `tls_key.pem`. When neither file of the pair exists the first start makes a self-signed ECDSA P-256 pair for `localhost` and the bind / advertised addresses; the key file is created owner-only (0600 on unix; on Windows it inherits the folder's access list). One file without the other refuses to start (nothing is overwritten). The key is never logged. | DB folder | none (ours) | `--tls-dir` | `tls::load_or_create` |
| LG-222 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **The fingerprint.** Every start logs the SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate (upper-case hex pairs joined by `:`) and the line `--server-fingerprint <fp>` to give to players; `dc-lobby-server tls [--db PATH] [--tls-dir DIR]` prints it (making the pair when missing). | as stated | none (ours) | none | `tls::startup_lines`, `tls::run_subcommand` |
| LG-223 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **One port, both kinds.** The auth and web ports look at the first two bytes of a connection: `0x16 0x03` (a TLS handshake record) starts TLS, anything else is a plain connection (the 2009 client's first auth frame is 0x206 or 0x200). The first bytes and the handshake must arrive within 10 s. The same port numbers as before. One deadline of 10 s covers the first bytes and the whole handshake together (a client sending a byte now and then is dropped at it), with a write timeout; at most 64 connections per listener may be in that phase at once, further ones are closed at once with a log line. | 10 s, 64 | none (ours) | none | `tls::admit` |
| LG-224 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **No clear password across the network.** On a public lobby (`--public`, or a non-loopback `--bind`) a plain connection from a non-loopback peer is closed on the auth port before any frame is read; on the web port a plain GET / HEAD gets `301` to the same address over `https://`, any other plain request `403`. Loopback peers (the host's own client and bots) may stay plain; "loopback" is the socket peer, so a same-host reverse proxy / tunnel / forwarder makes remote peers look local and needs `--tls loopback` (logged at start-up when `--public` is on and `--tls` is not `loopback`). A public lobby that cannot load or make its certificate does not start. `--plain-auth-public` lifts the refusal (the real 2009 client over a trusted network) and logs a loud warning three times. | on for public lobbies | none (ours) | `--plain-auth-public` | `tls::Gate`, `net::admit_and_serve`, `clanweb::redirect_to_tls`, `main::tls_gate` |
| LG-225 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **`--tls loopback`.** Plain connections are refused from every peer, loopback included (tests, and `play_rust.py` for dc-client sessions, so the TLS path runs every day). `--tls auto` (the default) is LG-224. | auto | none (ours) | `--tls auto\|loopback` | `tls::TlsMode` |
| LG-226 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **Plain lobby and clan ports.** The lobby port (auth + 2) and the clan port carry the session key from the server pick but no password; they stay plain for now (the 2009 client's lobby connection, and the bots' handed-over lobby link). A later task may wrap them the same way. | plain | none (ours) | none | `main` |
| CLI-1470 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **TLS client.** dc-client and dc-botclient open the auth connection (`TcpLink::connect_auth`) and the web port fetches (`clan_web_get`) with TLS 1.3 first. A loopback server that does not speak TLS gets a plain connection after the failed handshake (2 s at most on loopback; the reference stack, old test servers); a non-loopback server without TLS is refused: the password is never sent in clear. Without a pin and without a CA-issued certificate the client trusts on first use: the fingerprint of the first certificate seen for `host:port` is written to `known_servers.txt` in the profile folder (`DC_PROFILE_DIR`, else `%APPDATA%\DeCombat`) once the handshake has passed (written through a temporary file and a rename; a line of the file that does not parse is damage and the connection to that host is refused with "delete <path> to trust the server again" instead of a first use; a failed save is logged once and shown as a warning); the bots and tools without a profile keep it for the process only. | as stated | none (ours) | none | `dc_botclient::tls::connect_with` |
| CLI-1471 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **Pinning and the identity box.** `--server-fingerprint SHA256` (dc-client; or `DC_SERVER_FINGERPRINT` for dc-client and dc-botclient; any of `AB:CD..`, plain hex, `SHA256:..`) pins the server: a certificate with another fingerprint is refused, a matching one replaces the remembered fingerprint. A remembered fingerprint that no longer matches is refused. The login screen shows the refusal in an error box with the first line of the text ("The server's identity has changed. Ask the host for the new fingerprint and start the game with --server-fingerprint." / "... does not match the fingerprint you were given ..." / "This server does not offer an encrypted login, so DeCombat will not send your password ..."); the server address and both fingerprints go to the console. Continuing needs the new fingerprint on the command line; nothing is accepted by a click. | as stated | none (ours) | `--server-fingerprint`, `DC_SERVER_FINGERPRINT` | `dc_botclient::tls::Verifier`, `menu::login` |
| CLI-1472 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **Loopback servers.** A server on a loopback address is accepted with any certificate unless a pin is given (the traffic never leaves the machine; test lobbies make a new pair per run). | as stated | none (ours) | none | `dc_botclient::tls::Verifier` |
| CLI-1473 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **CA-issued certificates.** Without a pin a certificate chain that the operating system's trusted roots validate for the host name is accepted without trust on first use (`rustls-native-certs`: the same store the user's browser trusts; chosen over the bundled `webpki-roots` list, whose CA data is CDLA-Permissive-2.0 and goes stale). The host name is the one typed in `--lobby name:port`; an address typed as an IP is checked as an IP. | as stated | none (ours) | none | `dc_botclient::tls::native_roots`, `note_host` |
| CLI-1474 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **`DC_CLIENT_TLS=off`.** A support switch: plain connections to loopback servers without trying TLS; a non-loopback server is refused as without TLS. | auto | none (ours) | `DC_CLIENT_TLS` | `dc_botclient::tls::Mode` |
| CLI-1475 (proposed; deviation from 2009) | **TLS 1.3 only, https registration link.** Both ends are ours and browsers speak TLS 1.3, so TLS 1.2 is not offered. ## Held keys and the modifier state (crouch-walk-state, 2026-10-30)

Branch `crouch-walk-state` (wa). Ids CLI-1520 .. CLI-1521. User report on a9eac51d: after crouch (Ctrl) + walk (Alt)
+ fire, crouch or walk sometimes stayed held after the keys were let go. The 2009 commands are held: crouch is
command 5 / 0x5c on (MOVEMENT_2009 §5.1, §5.4 release rule), walk is our inverse of the held run command 7 (CLI-2;
§5.1 `RUN` = command 7 XOR the run lock, command 12 the only toggle). Both rules below keep that and only make the
held state follow the physical keys.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-1520 (proposed) | **An action is held while any of its keys is down.** The window sends each bound key as its own key (scan code, modifier family, action, down / up); a key-up releases only that key, the action stays held while another of its keys is down (C and Left Ctrl both crouch by default; the right Ctrl crouches by its logical key). A direct action event (scripted input) still holds / releases the action itself, and its release drops the keys of that action. | on | §5.1 (held commands; which keys is configuration) | none | `input::DeviceInput::Key`, `KeyboardMouse::device`, `window::key_input` |
| CLI-1521 (proposed) | **The modifier state releases stale modifier keys.** On every modifier-state change the window reports (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, logo), each held key of a family reported up is released, so a Ctrl or Alt key-up the platform never delivered (winit drops a Ctrl event it takes for the AltGr pair; a menu-mnemonic loop or an overlay hook can eat a key-up) cannot leave crouch or walk held. The right Alt of an AltGr layout is no Alt key (the platform reports Ctrl and Alt up while it is held), so it is never released this way; a Ctrl key held together with it is (a known edge, pressing it again holds it). | on | none (our rule; the 2009 engine read DirectInput key states, MOVEMENT_2009 §5.1) | none | `input::DeviceInput::Modifiers`, `window::modifiers_input` |

(cshell+0x2bd80) have no end sub and say nothing about the agent's death: no 2009 evidence for stage 2's end.

### net-overlay (user 2026-10-30: "an in-match network overlay toggled by /network")

Branch `net-overlay` (wb). Ids CLI-1570 .. CLI-1574. Our own feature: the 2009 client has no network overlay. Everything shown is computed locally from data the client already has; no message is added, nothing goes to the event log.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-1570 (proposed) | **`/network` command and its modes.** A chat line whose first word is `/network` or `/net` (any case) is handled by the client and never sent: alone it turns the overlay on (link block) or off; `/network 2` turns the players block on (or back to the link block); `/network off` / `0` turns it off; any other argument changes nothing. The mode is kept in our own profile section (`net_overlay = 0..2`) and the next match starts with it; `--net-overlay[=2]` or `DC_NET_OVERLAY=1|2` force the start mode for scripted runs. | off | ours | `net_overlay` (profile, own section), `--net-overlay`, `DC_NET_OVERLAY` | `hud::chat::local_command`, `hud::netview::next_mode`, `settings::{net_overlay_start, note_net_overlay}` |
| CLI-1571 (proposed) | **What the overlay measures.** A ring of 20 buckets of 250 ms (5 s) in the network thread: ping = mean / min / max of the client's own send-to-ack round trips (the transport's raw samples) over 5 s, else the 0xa2 value of the own player; jitter = their standard deviation; loss in = reliable block numbers skipped / numbers advanced (CLI-1572), loss out = resends / reliable blocks sent, both over 5 s; packets and kbit (UDP payload) per second over the last whole second; server update gap = arrival gap between stream time entries (mean and max over 5 s) and the age of the newest; playout delay and buffer depth = mean over the remote tracks of CLI-1330's drawn delay and of the samples not yet played; late / held = remote frames drawn past the newest sample / past CLI-1331's bound over 5 s; fps and frame time from the window's 120-frame meter. "felt" = ping + mean update gap + playout delay (the remote-movement part of docs/NET_LATENCY.md's budget). Refreshed every 250 ms. | 5 s, 250 ms, 1 s rates | ours | none (consts `meter::{BUCKET_MS, BUCKETS, RATE_BUCKETS}`, `netview::REFRESH_MS`) | `net::meter::NetMeter`, `NetWorld::net_sample`, `hud::netview::lines` |
| CLI-1572 (proposed) | **Receive sequence statistics.** The link counts, for each reliable block that is not discarded, how far it moves the highest block number seen (`rel_seq_span`) and how many numbers it skipped (`rel_seq_gaps`); a block filling an older gap counts nothing. Statistics only: the transport's behaviour is unchanged. | as stated | ours | none | `dc_net_engine::Link::note_rel_seq`, `LinkStats::{rel_seq_span, rel_seq_gaps}` |

Protocol: TLS 1.3 only, the lobby certificate accepted only when its DER SHA-256 equals the pin (no roots, no TOFU; the hello and its token are never sent to another certificate); hello answered within 15 s (connect / handshake 10 s); reconnect backoff 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s, 1 s after an accepted connection; `running` lines after every `ok`; `pong` for `ping`, own `ping` after 20 s without sending, close after 60 s of silence; lines over 16 KiB dropped with a log line both ways; nothing buffered while disconnected. Security: only `dserver_exe` runs, each argument its own argv entry (no shell): `-port -world -guid -idle -log <log_dir>/<log> -bindip <bind_ip>`, then `dserver_args`, then the lobby's `args` keeping flags (tokens starting with `-`) and the one non-flag value after each, dropping bare tokens and any repeat of the agent's own flags (these six, `-content`, and since 2026-11-01 `-worldfile`, `-announce`, `-worldobjects`: a lobby's `--dserver-args` no longer sets `-worldobjects` on a remote host, `host.toml` `dserver_args` does; MAP-83); `log` a plain file name (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, no leading dot, at most 128); `guid` alphanumeric; a requested port only inside `port_range`; port = requested if free, else the first of the range free for a UDP bind on `bind_ip` and not one of its own; `CA_ROM=<rom>`, working directory `log_dir`, own process group; `quit` closes stdin, the process group is killed 5 s later; exit code -1 = killed. An agent restart ends its game servers (the pipes cannot be taken over); a dropped connection does not. | as stated (ports 27888-27899, bind 0.0.0.0, log_dir `logs`, 16 KiB, 5 s, 10 / 15 / 20 / 60 s, backoff 1..30 s, token >= 24) | our own design (HOST_AGENT.md §2-§6; no 2009 host protocol is known); pipe contract DSERVER_PIPE.md §2 (argv, CA_ROM, 5 s grace); pin form LG-222 | `host.toml` keys; none for the timings | `dc_host::config::HostConfig::parse`, `dc_host::tls::PinVerifier`, `dc_host::proto::{filter_args, dserver_argv, LineBuf}`, `dc_host::ports::pick`, `dc_host::games::Games::{start, quit}`, `dc_host::link::session`; tests crates/dc-host (18 unit + 4 integration) |
