### identity-tokens (project decision: one identity, many ledgers; wa)

Branch `identity-tokens`. Ids LG-68, LG-69. Our own hosting design: no 2009 counterpart, no 2009 evidence needed.

| id | rule | default | evidence | override / config | hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LG-68 (proposed, project decision) | **Identity tokens: format, issuing, verification.** An issuing lobby (`--identity`, `identity.issue = true`, needs `identity.issuer`) keeps an Ed25519 key pair (PKCS#8 PEM `identity_key.pem` next to the DB, made on the first start, owner-only; `identity.key_file` / `--identity-key-file`), logs its public key (base64 of the raw 32 bytes) at start, and `dc-lobby-server identity --db FILE` prints it. Token = `b64url(payload) "." b64url(signature)` (RFC 4648 §5, no padding); payload = UTF-8 `dcid1\|<issuer id>\|<account u32>\|<login>\|<nick or empty>\|<issued unix s>\|<expires unix s>`, expires = issued + `identity.token_hours` x 3600; no field holds `\|` or a control character (a nick that would is left empty; such a login gets no token); issuer id 1..64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`. Issued by `POST /identity/token` on the web port with JSON `{"login","password"}`: 200 `{"token","expires","account","nick"}`; 401 `{"error":"wrong login or password"}` for an unknown name, a wrong password, a disabled account or an LG-146 lockout (failures counted as login failures); 404 when not issuing, 405 other methods, 400 not a JSON object. Valid when the signature verifies over the payload bytes, the issuer equals the configured one, issued <= now + 300 s and now <= expires + 300 s. A login carries it in the 0x200 login-name field (+6, wstr[4096]) as `tok:<token>` (`LOCAL:` prefix allowed); the password field is ignored (a wstr[17] cannot hold a token). A refused token gets the wrong-password reply (0x201 reason 0x00030025) and counts against the source address (LG-146). An account with an active ban gets no token (the endpoint answers the wrong-password 401), as the lobby would refuse it at login. | off; 24 h; 5 min skew | none (ours) | `identity.issue`, `identity.issuer`, `identity.public_key`, `identity.token_hours`, `identity.key_file`; `--identity`, `--identity-issuer`, `--identity-key`, `--identity-token-hours`, `--identity-key-file` | dc-lobby-server `identity::{sign, verify, route, from_options}`, `auth::token_login` |
| LG-69 (proposed, project decision) | **The local account of a token.** An accepting lobby (`identity.issuer` + `identity.public_key`) maps (issuer, account) through the `identity_links` table to one local account: the first token login makes a password-less account with the token's login name (also under `--no-auto-create`) and links it, later ones find it; the character, its progression and inventory stay this lobby's own (character creation as for any login; **amended 2026-11-01 by LG-273:** an identity login makes its character at once from the token's nick). A local account that already holds the login name (any case) without a link is not taken over: the login is refused with the wrong-password reply and a log line. A linked account has no password login (refused like a wrong password, loopback-exempt sessions excepted); the lobby's own unlinked accounts keep password logins. The issuing lobby takes its own tokens for its own account number (login name must match), without a link row. Disabled and banned accounts are refused as at any login. A token login also counts against, and is refused by, the per-name lockout of LG-146 for the name inside the token, as a password login of that name. | as stated | none (ours) | as LG-68 | dc-lobby-server `identity::local_account`, `db::{identity_link, link_identity, is_identity_linked}` |
| CLI-1610 (proposed, project decision) | **The client logs in once at the identity authority and joins lobbies with the token.** With the identity on (`--menu lobby`), the login screen's name + password go first to the authority: `POST /identity/token` with `{"login","password"}` over TLS (5 s limit). 200: the token is kept in memory and in the profile folder's `identity_token.json` (`token`, `expires`, `account`, `nick`, `login`, `authority`; written through a temporary file, owner-only on Unix, plain on Windows; never logged: the session log shows `tok:(hidden)`), and the lobby login carries the 0x200 login name `LOCAL:tok:<token>` with an empty password. A later start with an unexpired token of the same authority (expiry minus 60 s) puts its login name in the ID box with the keyboard on the login button; a login with that name and an empty password uses the token without asking the authority. A typed password always asks for a new token. A wrong-password reply (0x201 low word 0x25) to a token login deletes the cache and the screen asks for the password. 401 from the authority: the same wrong-password message; no answer / not issuing / a trust refusal: the connection-failure box (0x44f) or the trust box (CLI-1471), no lobby login. The authority: `--identity HOST:PORT` (`--identity-fingerprint SHA256` pins it; else trust on first use / a CA chain as CLI-1470), by default the lobby's host at the auth port + 8080 with the lobby's pin (`--server-fingerprint`); the default authority falls back to the plain password login when it answers 404 (the lobby does not issue) or, on a loopback lobby, when it does not answer (the password goes to that same host either way); a named one never falls back. `--identity off`: the plain password login (local accounts), as before. Register / Find ID / Find password use the authority's web port when the identity is on. The direct join (`--menu skip`) and dc-botclient keep password logins. | on (default authority) | none (ours, our own hosting design) | `--identity HOST:PORT\|off`, `--identity-fingerprint` | dc-client `identity::{resolve, request_token, store, load, clear}`, `menu::link::Worker::identity_login`, `menu::login::account_web`; tests `identity::tests::*`, `menu::link::tests::{a_password_login_becomes_a_token_login_at_the_lobby, a_cached_token_logs_in_without_the_password_and_a_refusal_drops_it, a_wrong_password_at_the_authority_is_the_wrong_password_outcome}` |

Each entry is resolved from `<mods_dir>/<sha256>.zip` (the file `/mods/<sha256>.zip` serves) when present: its SHA-256 must equal the declared one, it is unpacked (STORE zips as `dc-modkit pack` writes) into `<data dir>/mod_cache/<sha256>/` and loaded from there; otherwise from the folder `<mods_dir>/<id>/` when its deterministic pack hashes to the declared sha256. ## Client mod delivery (client-mod-runtime, 2026-11-01)

Branch `client-mod-runtime` (wb). Ids CLI-1608 .. CLI-1609. Our own feature (the 2009 client has no mods); the design is HOSTING_AND_MODS.md §4 and §8 items 1-2 (decided 2026-10-24) and docs/MODDING_GUIDE.md §7 and §10. The browser screen that shows the state is a later task, and so is the wire field that carries the hash at login.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-1608 (proposed) | **Cache and download rules.** Before each login the client reads `GET /server_list.json` from the lobby's web port (auth port + 8080, or `DC_CLANWEB`; at most 64 KiB, through the TLS connector, plain only on loopback). A `mod_set_hash` that differs from the hash of the listed set refuses the join. A `404` (a lobby without a server list) means vanilla. If the web port does not answer, the join goes on as vanilla only when the player's server-list entry says plain vanilla, or when there is no entry at all (a direct address): the client then sends the empty-set hash and loads nothing, and a modded server refuses that hash at login. A modded entry fails the join. An entry, when there is one, pins the policy and the hash: a lobby set that differs from it refuses the join. Only mods with `requires_client` are fetched (server_rules mods run on the server only, but they are still part of the hash). Each package comes from `<data>/mods/by-hash/<sha256>.zip` when its bytes still hash to the name; otherwise it is downloaded from `/mods/<sha256>.zip`, with a cap of 32 MiB per package (Content-Length and the bytes read), and hashed in memory **before** it is written under its name (written to `.part`, then renamed). A mismatch refuses the join and writes nothing. A verified zip is unpacked into `<data>/mods/unpacked/<sha256>/` (built in a `.part` folder, then renamed). Only stored entries are accepted, as `dc-modkit pack` writes them; the reader refuses compression, encryption, symlinks (unix mode 0120000), absolute paths, drive letters, backslashes, `.`/`..`/empty components, control characters, duplicate names, a bad CRC, more than 4096 entries, and an unpacked total over the per-package cap. The mods load into a new `ModHost` in the server's order as `ModOrigin::Server` under `Modded { client_visual_allowed }`. A package whose manifest id or version differs from its entry refuses the join. When the server allows local client-visual mods, `<data>/mods/local/*` loads as `ModOrigin::Local`; the host's refusals (any kind but client_visual, render or HUD hooks) are kept as messages and do not fail the join. Afterwards the cache is trimmed, least recently used first (by file modification time, refreshed on each cache hit), to 256 MiB. The packages of the current set are never removed, and a removed package's unpacked folder goes with it. A failure keeps its reason in the link's mod status, shows the login-failed box, and the login request is not sent. `<data>` is the profile folder (CLI-553); with no profile folder, a modded server cannot be joined. | on | HOSTING_AND_MODS.md §4 items 2-5, §8 item 2; MODDING_GUIDE.md §7 items 2-4. The design gives no number for the client's size caps or for the unreachable-port case, so these are ours: the lobby's own send cap is `mods.max_zip_bytes`, 32 MiB by default, the client's cap too (MOD-29). Zip layout: PKWARE APPNOTE (public). Tests dc-client `mods::tests::*` | `LinkOptions::mods` (`ModConfig`: `max_mod_bytes`, `cache_bytes`, `timeout`, `data_dir`) | `dc_client::mods` (`ClientMods::join`, `fetch_set`, `read_package`, `trim_cache`), `menu::link::Worker::mod_step`, `LinkCmd::ExpectModSet`, `LinkEvent::Mods` |
| CLI-1609 (proposed) | **Vanilla unloads everything; the set hash.** Every login first drops the previous sandbox, so leaving a server unloads its mods (the cache stays). On a vanilla policy the client keeps no `ModHost` at all, so no mod is loaded, local client-visual mods included, and the hash is the empty-set hash (`e3b0c442...b855`). On a modded policy the hash is the SHA-256 of one line `id@version:sha256` and a line feed per declared mod whose kind is not `client_visual`, in the server's order: the same text as the lobby's (one implementation, `dc_mod_lua::mod_set_hash_text`, now used by both). The hash of a successful mod step is kept in `Worker::mod_set_hash` and `Link::join_report().hash`, for the login. | on | HOSTING_AND_MODS.md §4 item 6, §8 item 1; MODDING_GUIDE.md §10. Tests `vanilla_unloads_a_loaded_local_mod_and_yields_the_empty_set_hash`, `a_set_of_one_mod_downloads_verifies_unpacks_loads_and_hashes_like_the_lobby`, dc-mod-lua `modset::tests` | none | `ServerModSet::hash`, `ClientMods::unload` |

Team texts `"1"` / `"2"` (`""` = any where allowed); `modes` a comma list of the lobby's playable mode names, empty = every mode; `extent` HALF extents (flags 0x4). The ROM roles without a `dc.*` name (trigger volume, mode controller, start-up command, camera point, doors, switches, water, placed effects) cannot be placed by a community map (D12). | MAP-2 (DC-DEFAULT proposed; project decision dc-mapkit, plan §4 / §6.1) | **Alias matching.** Every reader identifies a class, property or text value through `dc_world::Key { hash, len, ours }`: the name matches when its `(sha256(name)[:8], len)` equals the ROM key exactly, OR when it equals `ours` ignoring ASCII case; a key with an empty `ours` is ROM-only and a key with no ROM counterpart (`sky_inner`) has a zero hash that no name reaches. `ObjectRole::of_class` and `Object::is_class` apply both halves to a class name on any object; `Object::prop_by_key` / `prop_named` (and the typed reads over them) apply the hash half on every object and the `ours` half ONLY on a vocabulary object, one whose class is a `dc.*` name (`names::is_dc_class`, kept as `Object::dc` from the parse): a ROM object's properties resolve by hash alone, so a ROM property that happens to spell a vocabulary word (the ROM's `rayhit`-, `team`-, `color`- and `radius`-like names on kill volumes, ladders, water, flag zones, sprites and lights, 3,546 (object, key) misfires over the 21 ROM worlds before, review C5) is never taken for the vocabulary key. One world may still mix ROM-hashed and `dc.*` objects and each resolves on its own. Property 0 / 1 / 2 are read by index (FMT_DAT85.md §6.1), the names `name` / `pos` / `rot` being aliases. One vocabulary word may be a different ROM property per class (`team`: team filter on spawns and flags, zone team on flag zones; `color`: light vs sprite colour; `file`: sound vs sprite file; `model` and the sprite `file` are the same ROM property): the reader uses the per-site key (`names::PROP_TEAM_FILTER` vs `PROP_TEAM`, `PROP_LIGHT_COLOR` vs `PROP_SPRITE_COLOR`, `PROP_SOUND_FILE` vs `PROP_SPRITE_FILE`, `PROP_MODEL`). Keys, no others (an unknown key names the list): required `id` (the map key, `a-z 0-9 _`, 1..32), `name` (1..48 characters, no control characters), `world` (this mod's own asset `@mod:<mod id>/assets/...dat`, exactly as `mod.assets:path("assets/...")` returns it), `modes` (a non-empty list of `dc_config::modes::MODE_NAMES` spelled as listed, no duplicates); optional `description` (<= 400 characters), `goals` (table mode name -> positive whole number; only modes of `modes`), `round_seconds` (whole, 30..3600), `picture` and `loading` (non-empty texture path strings: a ROM path or `mod.assets:path`), `radar` (`{ picture, min = { x, z }, max = { x, z } }`, finite numbers, min below max on both axes), `players` (`{ min, max }`, whole 1..16, min <= max). `:patch(id, partial)` merges into a record some loaded mod registered: a deep merge, except that `modes`, `goals`, `players` and `radar` are replaced whole when the partial carries them (lists are values: `{ modes = { "FFA" } }` leaves exactly FFA, so a patch can shrink the mode list and must then carry `goals` for the new list; a partial `radar` is refused as incomplete); a patch of an unregistered key is refused; `id` may not change; the merged record is checked again against the OWNER's assets, so the world stays the registering mod's file. `:override` is refused for the domain. A mod whose entry fails after registering (an error, a second bad record, a capability denial caught with `pcall`) is rolled back with its hooks and listeners: in every content domain its `:register`ed records (record, owner, key) and the content of its `:patch` calls (the records are restored, its name leaves the patcher lists) are removed, so it reserves no map key and a later mod may register it. `ModHost::map_records()` returns the records of the LOADED mods as `MapRecord` plain data (`mod_id` = the registering mod, `patched_by` = the mods that patched it in load order, the fields above with `goals` sorted by mode) ordered by the registering mod's load position, then by map key; a record whose owner is not loaded is skipped (defensive, the rollback leaves none), a loaded mod's record that fails the check there (not reachable through Lua) is an `Err` a lobby treats like a malformed declared set. | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.4; the key limits are the room list's and the 0x311 map table's practical sizes, the player cap is `max_players_cap` 16; the review of 2026-11-01 C9 (stale records of a failed mod) and C12 (a patch could not shrink `modes`)) | none | `dc_mod_lua::mapkeys::{check_map_record, MAP_RECORD_KEYS, MAP_REPLACED_KEYS, MAP_ID_MAX, MAP_NAME_MAX, MAP_DESCRIPTION_MAX, ROUND_SECONDS_RANGE, PLAYERS_RANGE}`, `maprecord::{MapRecord, RadarInfo, PlayerRange}`, `ModHost::map_records`, `host::ContentDomainStore::patch_undo` (`remove_registrations` / `commit_registrations`), `CONTENT_DOMAINS`; tests dc-mod-lua `mapkeys::tests`, `maprecord::tests`, `kind_tests::{a_map_record_round_trips_through_register, a_bad_map_record_refuses_the_mod_with_the_rule_in_the_message_even_under_pcall, map_records_come_in_load_order_then_key_order_and_patches_merge_into_the_owners_record, a_mod_that_fails_after_registering_a_map_leaves_no_record_and_frees_its_key, a_map_patch_replaces_modes_goals_players_and_radar_whole}` |

| MAP-10 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Project format 1.** A map is a folder: `map.json` (serde-typed `Project`, `"format": 1`, unknown keys refused), `terrain.r16` (little-endian u16 heights, row-major with row = z, over the vertex grid `(cells_x + 1) x (cells_z + 1)`; world y = `origin[1] + raw / 65535 * height_scale`; absent file = flat at raw 0), `assets/` (own textures, OBJ meshes), `AGENTS.md`, `.gitignore` (`build/`, `.mapkit/`). ## Community map builder, stage 2: the renderer reads the vocabulary and draws the editor viewport (mapkit-stage2, 2026-11-01)

Branch `mapkit-stage2` (docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md 6.2 for dc-render and D7). Ids MAP-26 .. MAP-28. Our own feature (the
2009 client cannot play a community map; the viewport is the dc-mapkit editor's). The keys are `dc_world::names`
(MAP-1 / MAP-2); this section only says how dc-render applies them and what the GUI draws into.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAP-26 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; MAPKIT_PLAN.md 6.2) | **dc-render reads the vocabulary through `Key::matches`.** Every class, property and value the renderer compares against is a `dc_world::names::Key`, so a `dc.*` object reads exactly like its ROM twin: `fog.rs` (`PROP_FOG_ENABLE`, `PROP_FOG_NEAR`, `PROP_FOG_FAR`, `PROP_FOG_COLOR`, `PROP_SKY_FOG_NEAR`, `PROP_SKY_FOG_FAR` on the `dc.world_settings` object: the world-settings role object first, else the first object with the fog enable; the sky pass fogged under the world's enable, colour truncated to 0..255, near == far off, as before), `lights.rs` (`CLASS_POINT_LIGHT` = `dc.point_light`, `CLASS_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHT` / `CLASS_OBJECT_LIGHT` ROM-only, `CLASS_GLOBAL_LIGHT` = `dc.global_light`; `PROP_LIGHTS_OBJECTS` true and `PROP_RADIUS` > 0 required for a static light, `PROP_LIGHT_COLOR` = `color`, `PROP_BRIGHT`, `PROP_TO_AMBIENT`, `PROP_CONE`; ROM-only and so hash-matched only: the inner colour, the object bright scale, the fast-lights flag, the attenuation coefficients / exponents / kind and its three values, so a `dc.point_light` always gets the dynamic law `1 / (1 + 19 d^2 / r^2)`), `scene.rs` (`PROP_VISIBLE`, `PROP_BLEND` with `BLEND_OPAQUE` / `BLEND_ADDITIVE` (any other value, `translucent` included, blends with alpha), `PROP_ALPHA`; `PROP_HIDDEN` / `PROP_START_HIDDEN` ROM-only). The read ORDER of every reader is unchanged: `static_light` takes the colour, then the inner colour; `global_light` the inner colour, then the colour (a `dc.global_light` carries `color` only, so it lands on the alternative in both). The hex-string key form is gone from these three files; names are matched ASCII-case-insensitively on the `ours` half only (MAP-2). | as stated | ours (the hashes are the ones these files held before; ROM-gated `rom_styles::rom_global_light_and_light_group_grids`, `rom_fog`, `rom_maps` unchanged) | none | `dc_render::{world_fog, global_light, global_light_count, light_class, static_light, world_lights, model_visibility}`; tests `tests/dc_vocab_render.rs::{dc_world_settings_yields_the_fog_of_both_passes, dc_global_light_yields_the_sun, dc_point_light_needs_lights_objects_and_a_radius, dc_world_model_blend_classifies_the_model}` |
| MAP-27 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; MAPKIT_PLAN.md D7) | **The editor viewport target.** `OffscreenTarget::new(ctx, format, samples, size)` (or `for_renderer(ctx, &renderer, size)`) is a single-sample colour texture of the renderer's colour format (`OFFSCREEN_FORMAT` = `Rgba8Unorm` headless; `format()` reports it) made with `RENDER_ATTACHMENT | TEXTURE_BINDING | COPY_SRC`, a Depth32Float depth texture, and, for a sample count above 1, the multisampled colour + depth pair of `MsaaTargets`; sizes are clamped to at least 1 x 1. `WorldRenderer::render_frame_to_target(ctx, scene, camera, opts, models, view_models, pv, xray, &target)` records the SAME passes as `render_frame_offscreen_xray` (sky, world, models, translucent objects, eye-attached models, the x-ray pass when asked; with MSAA on the frame's last 3D pass resolves into the colour texture, CLI-1593), submits them and returns the `FrameReport` WITHOUT waiting (`gpu_ms` 0): the caller samples `view()` from a later pass on the same queue (the GUI's `egui::PaintCallback`) and the submission order makes the frame complete by then. `resize(ctx, size)` remakes the textures only when the size changed (true, `generation()` + 1: a registered view must be registered again); `read_back(ctx)` copies the colour texture out through the one shared read-back (`unpack_rows`, alpha 255, BGRA swapped for a window format), blocking, so a viewport screenshot is the same bytes as the read-back path's frame. `frame_target(resolves)` is the `FrameTarget` of one pass for callers that record their own passes into the same target. When the first solid along a reported shot (the DSV-34 trace) is a sky face, the shot is refused like at any wall (a claimed hit behind it does no damage) but the effect record is the NO-HIT record (`first` none, mask miss) ending at the sky point and carrying the SKY surface id `dc_world::SURFACE_SKY` (0x6e: the id the client's impact guard skips, so no decal, impact effect or sound lands on the sky on any client; before review C4 the record carried the fallback world surface 71, which the client draws); the same for a miss whose first wall is a sky face. A plain wall keeps the world surface. The continuation record of a hit on a character (DSV-86) is not sent when the wall behind the victim is a sky face. The sky face's `texflags` never reach the server's record, but the shooter's own client traces the face itself and reads its `texflags` as the surface, so a built sky face must carry `SURFACE_SKY` as its `texflags` too (every ROM sky surface does; dc-mapkit's sky faces, the build half of C4). The one number lives in dc-world (`SURFACE_SKY`, the client's `fx.rs SURFACE_SKY` is the same value, `gs::SURFACE_SKY` its byte). A sky face in a brush model is not special (brushes are not in the shot trace). | as stated | ours (open point 2 of the plan; the client's sun test needs the solid 0x10 face, so the face must stay solid) | `combat.trace` (DSV-34; off = no trace, no rule) | `dc_world::SURFACE_SKY`, `dc_dserver::gs::SURFACE_SKY`, `dc_dserver::game::Game::{wall_hit_along, shot_effect, shot_exit}`, `world::SURF_SKY`; tests `game::tests::shots_into_a_sky_face_answer_the_no_hit_record` (the record's surface byte is the sky id), `game::tests::shots_through_a_wall_are_refused_and_end_at_it` (a wall is not), `dc_world tests/dc_vocab.rs::rom_worlds_resolve_through_the_hash_half` (ROM-gated: every ROM sky surface's `texflags` equals `SURFACE_SKY`) |
| MAP-25 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **What makes an object a vocabulary object, and the movers' keys.** `world::is_dc_object(o)` is true when the object's role class key matches the class name through the alias half (`Key::matches_ours`: `dc.player_spawn`, `dc.capture_flag`, ...), never through the ROM hash; an object without a role is not one (sounds, sprites, lights carry no mode or team rule). It is `dc_world::Object::dc` (MAP-2, the gate of the own property names) narrowed to the role classes. `WorldInfo.spawn_dc` (index-aligned with `spawns`) and `FlagInfo.dc` carry it to the game layer. dc-sim's `WorldFilter.movers` is a `Vec<dc_world::Key>` (`is_mover` = any key matches the class name), so a client or test lists a mover class by hash or by an own name; the default is `names::MOVER_CLASSES` (sliding door, rotating door, rotating switch; ROM-only, scope cut D12). | as stated | ours (MAP-2) | none | `dc_dserver::world::{is_dc_object, WorldInfo.spawn_dc, FlagInfo.dc}`, `dc_sim::from_world::{WorldFilter.movers, WorldFilter::is_mover}`; tests `world::tests::dc_world_resolves_through_the_vocabulary`, `from_world::pose_tests::the_default_filter_takes_the_movers` |

## Community map builder, stage 2: the BSP builder (mapkit-stage2 bsp, 2026-11-01)

Branch `mapkit-stage2` (plan docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md D5, 5.3 step 3 as amended by the review: `crates/dc-mapkit/src/bsp.rs`). Our own builder (the 2009 engine's tree shape is observed only through the ROM census in the plan: 1.6-2.6 nodes per polygon, no shared children, -2 / -1 sentinels); ids MAP-40 .. MAP-42.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAP-40 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Tree shape.** `bsp::build` makes the node tree the collision walk needs (`dc-sim` walks nodes, never the polygon list) in two phases. Phase 1, only with `helpers` on: a cell with more than `cell_polys` polygons is split by an axis-aligned plane chosen among the quantiles (1/4, 1/2, 3/4) of the polygons' per-axis minimum and maximum bounds on x, y and z, minimising the larger child (straddlers count on both sides), ties by fewer straddlers, then axis x, y, z and position; on a terrain grid every candidate is a grid line, so no grid triangle straddles. A split that makes no progress ends phase 1 for that cell, as does `max_depth` helper splits on the path. **Node budget** (amended 2026-11-01, review C13): phase 2 duplicates a straddler into both subtrees without clipping, so k polygons that straddle every candidate plane of one cell (long rotated walls through a common area: the kd phase makes no progress on them) make about 2^k nodes; `bsp::build` therefore counts the naive-phase nodes per cell and stops when a cell passes `max(64, 16 x its polygons)` (`CELL_BUDGET_MIN`, `CELL_BUDGET_PER_POLY`) or the whole tree passes `16 x polygons` (`TREE_BUDGET_PER_POLY`), returning the tree so far with `BspTree::budget_exceeded = Some(BudgetHit { cell_polys, nodes })` (`cell_peak` reports the heaviest cell of any build); the build turns it into the error `bsp.budget` naming the solids / imports the cell's polygons came from (`geom::Level::poly_sources`) and advising to split or realign them. Measured with the budget off: every box, slope and heightfield set of the suite peaks at 16 .. 37 nodes for a 13 .. 16 polygon cell; the review's passing probe set (12 x 12 heightfield, two cylinders, three 5,000-unit diagonals) peaks at 146 nodes for a 16-polygon cell, hence 16 x n rather than 8 x n; the hanging probe (6 .. 20 walls 5,000 x 600 x 8 through one point) needs 1,152 .. millions of nodes for 36 .. 120 polygons and is refused from 6 walls on. Limitation: a map whose long rotated walls all cross one area must split them (or make them brushes); the builder does not clip. The split node references a **helper polygon**: 0 corners, surface flags 0, texflags 0, an exact unit axis normal with `d` at the split; the walk takes only its plane from it (flags 0 = never swept). Phase 2: a naive polygon BSP over the cell: splitter = the polygon whose plane straddles the fewest others (ties: fewest behind, then input order; at most 24 candidates scored, evenly strided), plane test with EPS 0.01 as `dc_sim::build_bsp` (a corner farther than EPS in front / behind puts the polygon there, both = straddler referenced from BOTH subtrees without clipping, coplanar = positive side). Every polygon of the input, solid or not, is referenced by at least one node; the tree is a tree (no shared children, no cycle), nodes are in pre-order with the root first. Node convention: `neg` = child behind the node polygon's plane, `pos` = in front; missing `neg` = -2, missing `pos` = -1; the file's `node_front` field carries the NEGATIVE child and `node_back` the positive one (`bsp::file_nodes`, `dc_sim::from_world::FILE_FIRST_CHILD_IS_NEGATIVE`); an empty input has no node and root -1. Measured: a 64 x 64 heightfield (8,192 triangles) gives 8,703 nodes (511 helpers), depth 20; 49,928 triangles give 56,814 nodes, depth 25, in 0.62 s in a debug build. | `BspOptions { cell_polys: 16, helpers: true, max_depth: 64 }`; `map.json` `build.cell_polys` (16) feeds `cell_polys` | plan D5; dc-sim collide.rs `CollModel::sweep` (node plane + SURF_SOLID gate), `build_bsp` (EPS, coplanar, straddlers); from_world.rs FILE_FIRST_CHILD_IS_NEGATIVE | `build.cell_polys` | crates/dc-mapkit/src/bsp.rs `build`, `kd_split`, `choose_splitter`, `partition`, `file_nodes` |
| MAP-41 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Helpers only in the level model; brushes get the naive tree.** Helper polygons may appear only in a model no object names (the level): the sweep ignores a flags-0 node polygon, but a ladder volume takes EVERY polygon plane of its brush (`dc-sim from_world.rs brush_volume`) and a kill volume every polygon with >= 3 corners (dserver killvol.rs), so a helper inside a brush model would bound the ladder region wrongly or inflate the model box. Brush models (kill volumes, ladders, world models, breakables, the sky model) are built with `BspOptions::brush()` = `helpers: false`: phase 2 alone over the whole brush (<= 24 candidates per level keeps it polynomial for a big brush), no helper polygon ever written; a model an object names never carries a flags-0 polygon (the build-time validator rule of plan 5.3 step 3). | level: `helpers: true`; brushes: `BspOptions::brush()` | review finding 7 (helpers break ladders / kill volumes); plan 5.3 step 3 as amended | none | crates/dc-mapkit/src/bsp.rs `BspOptions::brush`, test `every_polygon_is_referenced_and_no_helper_without_the_option` |
| MAP-42 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Verification suite** (no ROM, synthetic geometry only). `bsp::check` reports: a malformed helper (corners, flags, surface, non-axis plane), a polygon index past input + helpers, a child index out of range or the wrong sentinel for its side, a self reference, a node referenced other than exactly once from the root (shared child, unreachable, cycle), a solid polygon referenced by no node, depth above 1,024 (our own bound; the walk's stack spills to the heap and has none). The unit tests compare, for random boxes (grid-snapped and free), floors with one-sided ramps of several pitches and a sloped ceiling, a 32 x 32 heightfield and the heightfield with blocks on it, thousands of random body sweeps (three cylinder sizes, moves of 0.5 .. 9,000 units), rays and overlap tests between a `dc_sim::CollModel` built from our tree THROUGH THE FILE (`SynthModel` -> `World::parse` + `check_layout` -> `collision_world`, so the file convention of MAP-40 is what is tested) and one built by `dc_sim::build_bsp`: presence must be identical and a hit must be at the same instant; two faces reached at the same raw time (a shared edge or vertex, two faces of one plane, a start already overlapping geometry) come in walk order (the first visited wins the walk's strict `<`) and the 0.1-unit back-off along their different contact normals then moves the reported `t` by its last digits, so a hit within half a unit along the move (`|dt| * len <= 0.5`) that differs in polygon, normal, face normal or flags counts as a tie, at most 5 % of hits (on a heightfield every edge is shared and a wide cylinder rim often lands on one; the box and slope sets show 0); a hit farther apart than that, or one tree hitting where the other does not, is a failure. Added 2026-11-01 (review C13): `sweep_equality_rotated_solids` runs the same equality over rotated boxes, 1-unit walls and 0.5-unit slabs, 24- and 16-sided cylinders with three spanning diagonals over a heightfield, and rotated wedges and prisms (0 mismatches, as the review's probe found), and `mutually_crossing_rotated_walls_stop_at_the_budget_instead_of_hanging` pins that 20 walls through one point answer `budget_exceeded` within seconds with a structurally sound partial tree, with and without helpers, while 4 such walls build and verify. Also pinned: every polygon referenced, no helper with `helpers: false`, 64 x 64 heightfield nodes <= 2.5 x polygons and depth <= 300 with every x / z helper on a grid line, a 50k-triangle heightfield builds in < 20 s (0.62 s measured; the 2 s target of the plan), determinism (two builds are equal), pre-order, the file node encoding. `dc-mapkit build` runs `check` on every model and the sweep checks on the written world (the build slice). | the suite runs in `cargo test -p dc-mapkit` | plan 5.3 steps 3 and 6; dc-sim collide.rs `pruned_rays_equal_the_sweep_in_random_box_worlds` pattern and tests/synthetic_world.rs `to_synth` | none | crates/dc-mapkit/src/bsp.rs `check`, `depth`, `stats`, tests `sweep_equality_*`, `heightfield_64_tree_shape`, `fifty_thousand_triangles_build_quickly`, `check_catches_broken_trees` |

### mapkit-stage2: the world build pipeline (2026-11-01, docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.3 steps 1-6, D6, section 4)

Ids MAP-43 .. MAP-48. Our own tool (no 2009 counterpart); the file layout follows FMT_DAT85.md and what the DeCombat
readers consume (dc-sim, dc-dserver, dc-render, dc-client), never the ROM's content.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAP-43 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The build pipeline and the file layout.** `dc-mapkit build <dir>` runs the project checks (MAP-13; an error refuses the build), assembles the geometry (`build::level_of`), bakes the vertex colours (MAP-44), builds one BSP per model (`bsp::build`: kd helper planes down to `build.cell_polys` polygons then a naive BSP for the level, the naive BSP alone for every brush: helpers live in the level model only, written as plane-only polygons with no corners, flags 0, texflags 0, after the real polygons), writes the world through `dc_world::synth::SynthWorld` and parses it back for the world-level checks (MAP-47); the file goes to `build/<key>.dat` (written even when those checks find errors; the exit code follows the diagnostics) and `--json` reports `{file, bytes, stats: {polys, brushes, sky_faces, nodes, depth, textures, vertices, triangles, sections, bytes}}`; `validate --world` builds in memory and runs the same checks writing nothing. Layout: models = the level first (`bsp_name` `level`, flags 0: terrain, plain solids, collision imports and the 0x10 sky faces, which are solid) then one model per brush solid in project order (`bsp_name` = the solid id, flags bit 1, `origin` = the solid's centre, geometry in world space, box from its corners; MAP-3); per model the points, planes and surfaces are deduplicated by bit pattern, a surface = (flags, texture index, texflags = the material's `surface_id`, EXCEPT that every sky face carries texflags `worldgen::SURFACE_SKY` = 0x6e whatever its material says: the ROM's 126 sky polygons all carry 110 and the client's impact guard (dc-client fx.rs `SURFACE_SKY`) recognises a sky hit by that id alone, so a shot into a community map's sky plays no impact and lays no mark; `check_world` refuses a 0x10 polygon with any other texflags, `sky.surface`; amended 2026-11-01, review C4; the constant moves to `dc_world::SURFACE_SKY` once the engine side lands), texture names sorted (MAP-45); nodes use the walk's convention (first child = the negative side, `-2` / `-1` for a missing negative / positive child, coplanar polygons on the positive side); objects = the project's objects (property values typed by `dc_world::vocab`: `number` and `sky_index` ints, `color` / `fog_color` rgb, `extent` a vec3 with flags 0x4, text, bool, else real; name = the object's `name` or its id; `rot` degrees -> radians) then one object per brush (MAP-46), then `dc.world_settings` and `dc.global_light` (MAP-46); render data = one top-level block for the level with kind-1 sections grouped by texture name in name order (every level polygon EXCEPT the sky faces; one vertex per polygon corner: position, uv by the face's dominant axis over the material's `tile`, uv1 0, ARGB colour, the plane normal, tangent / binormal 0; fan triangles in the polygon's stored order, which the renderer draws as front faces; triangle source = the polygon index), the sky faces as the block's `sky_portals` (plane-polys, world space), and one nested render world per drawn brush: world models and breakables as they are, the sky model with its faces turned inside (reversed order, negated normal), nothing for kill volumes and ladders; a 1 x 1 x 1 light grid of the ambient colour over the extents; the quadtree one leaf; no blind data, no blockers, no light-group grids; extents = the geometry box (every polygon of every model) grown by 128 units; info text `decombat mapkit v1`. An own texture outside `assets/` refuses the build (`texture.assets`). Ground snapping (MAP-11) ignores a level solid whose top face carries a sky material (the templates' sky lid) so a spawn never lands on the sky. Prefabs are still ignored (no library yet). | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.3 as amended by the 2026-11-01 review: helpers in the level only, sky faces out of the sections and into the portals; FMT_DAT85.md §5.2, §6.1, §10; dc-sim `FILE_FIRST_CHILD_IS_NEGATIVE`) | `build.cell_polys` (16) | `dc_mapkit::build::{build, Built, BuildStats, texture_names}`, `bsp::{build, BspTree, BspOptions, depth, check}` (placeholder; the bsp slice's builder replaces it), `worldgen::{bsp_model, render_world, vertex_bytes, map_object, brush_object, brush_render}`, `cli::verb_build`; tests `tests/build_templates.rs::every_template_builds_parses_and_passes_the_world_checks`, `worldgen::tests::*`, `bsp::tests::*`, the CLI smoke test |
| MAP-44 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The bake rule.** Vertex colours carry the world's light (no lightmaps): per polygon corner with the polygon's plane normal `n`, per channel `c`: `light = bake.ambient * ambient_c / 255 + bake.sun * sun_bright * sun_color_c / 255 * max(0, dot(n, -sun_dir)) + bake.hemisphere * (0.5 + 0.5 * n.y)`, then `light *= 1 - bake.ao * occlusion`, byte = `clamp(round(light * 128), 0, 255)`, written ARGB with alpha 0xFF (kind-1 sections draw `texture * colour * 2`, so 0x80 is unit brightness; the defaults put sunlit ground near 0x6A and a shaded wall near 0x1A). `occlusion` is a cheap terrain ambient occlusion: the mean over eight compass directions at `2 * cell_size` of `clamp((terrain height there - corner y) / distance, 0, 1)`, 0 without terrain, off the grid, or above the surroundings. Every term is a fixed sequence of f32 operations (no transcendental). Weights come from `build.bake` (`ambient` 0.35, `sun` 0.65, `hemisphere` 0.15, `ao` 0.5), colours and the sun from `settings` (`ambient`, `sun_color`, `sun_bright`, `sun_dir`). | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md D6, 5.3 step 2; RENDER_2009.md §5.2 kind 1 as read by dc-render) | `build.bake.{ambient, sun, hemisphere, ao}`, `settings.{ambient, sun_color, sun_bright, sun_dir}` | `dc_mapkit::bake::{BakeInput, colour_at, bake_poly, bake_polys, occlusion, sun_towards}`; tests `bake::tests::*` |
| MAP-45 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Texture names of own textures.** A material's texture name in the world's texture tables and render sections is the ROM path verbatim for `{"rom": path}`, and for `{"own": path}` the string `@mod:<mod_meta.id>/<path with its extension replaced by .dtx>` (`assets/ground.png` -> `@mod:my_map/assets/ground.dtx`; the replacement is `worldgen::dtx_rel_path`: the extension of the LAST path segment only, a segment without one or a dotfile keeps its whole name, so `assets/v1.0/ground` -> `assets/v1.0/ground.dtx` and `assets/.hidden` -> `assets/.hidden.dtx`; `export::dtx_path_of` calls the same function, amended 2026-11-01, review C19: the two used to diverge on those inputs and the client then found no file): the file `export` writes the converted DTX to inside the mod package, resolved by the client's mod asset layer (`@mod:` paths resolve under `assets/` only, so an own texture outside `assets/` is a build error). Texture names are listed sorted per model and sections are grouped by name, so two materials over one PNG share a section. | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md 6.3, D2; MODDING_GUIDE.md `@mod:` asset paths) | none | `dc_mapkit::worldgen::{texture_name, DTX_EXT}`, `build::texture_names`; tests `worldgen::tests::texture_names_follow_the_mod_rule`, `build::tests::own_textures_outside_assets_are_refused`, `tests/build_templates.rs::the_render_data_batches_by_texture_and_carries_the_sky` |
| MAP-46 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Generated objects.** Every brush solid gets the object that names its model (class from the role, `name` = the solid id, `pos` = the solid's centre, `rot` 0): `dc.world_model` with `visible`, `solid`, `rayhit` true; `dc.breakable` the same plus `hit_points` 100 (the project has no field for it yet); `dc.kill_volume` and `dc.ladder` with no property (the kill is immediate; the ladder is climbable by its kind); `dc.sky_model` with `sky_index` 0, `sky_dims` = half its box and `sky_inner` 0.9 on every axis. ## Community map builder, stage 2: export, software render, ROM listings (mapkit-stage2, 2026-11-01)

Branch `mapkit-stage2` (docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.2 `export` / `render` / `rom`, 5.3 step 7, D8 render rules, the ROM discovery MAP rule). Our own tool; ids MAP-50 .. MAP-55. Code: `crates/dc-mapkit/src/{export,render_sw,romlist,thumbs}.rs`.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAP-50 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Export layout and record generation.** `dc-mapkit export <dir> [--zip] [--no-rom-paths]` builds the world and writes `build/mod/<mod_meta.id>/` from scratch (a previous export is removed first): `manifest.json` (kind `shared`, capabilities `assets` + `content.maps`, `name` = the project name, `version` / `description` / `author` / `tags` / `homepage` from `mod_meta`, `screenshots = ["screenshots/main.png"]`), `main.lua` (one `mod.content.maps:register{...}` call: `id` = the project key, `name` cut to 48 characters, `description` cut to 400, `world = mod.assets:path("assets/maps/<key>.dat")`, `modes` = the project's mode names upper-cased and kept only when they are DeCombat mode names (an unknown one is dropped with `mode.unknown`; none left is `meta.invalid`), `goals` for the listed modes, `round_seconds` and `players` when set, `picture` / `loading` only when the project ships `assets/pictures/<key>.png` / `<key>_load.png`, `radar` always), `assets/maps/<key>.dat`, the own textures (MAP-51), the pictures (MAP-52) and a generated `README.md`. The folder is then validated, linted and packed by `dc_modkit::pack_mod_bytes` (the lobby hashes the same bytes): a refusal is `export.pack` with dc-modkit's lines; `--zip` writes `build/<mod id>.zip`; the answer carries `dir`, `zip`, `sha256`, `files`, `bytes`. `--no-rom-paths` refuses a project with any `{"rom": ...}` texture (`export.rom_path`; CLEANROOM §4, committed examples); without it a ROM texture path is warned `rom.unverified` (not shipped; the client resolves it from its ROM). The world's own texture names (`@mod:<id>/assets/...`) are checked against the files written (`texture.missing` warning). The real folder size is compared with the caps: from 28 MiB `size.estimate` (warning, MOD-29), above 32 MiB `size.limit` (error, nothing packed). A build whose world-level checks reported errors (`bsp.unreferenced`, `killvol.closed`, `ladder.convex`, `world.level`, `extent.limit`, `sky.surface`, ...) is refused before anything is written, the answer being the build's diagnostics plus `build.fail` "nothing exported" and the JSON envelope `ok: false`, unless `--force` (`ExportOptions::force`) is given; the MCP `export` tool gains the same flag (amended 2026-11-01, review C18). An invalid mod id / version / description / author / key is refused before anything is written (`meta.invalid`, `project.key`). | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.3 step 7, 5.4, D2; dc-mod-lua `check_map_record`, manifest rules) | none | `dc_mapkit::export::{export, ExportOptions, Exported, lua_str}`; tests `export::tests::a_flat_template_exports_to_a_packable_shared_mod_twice_the_same`, `rom_paths_are_refused_with_the_flag_and_warned_without_and_missing_textures_are_named` |
| MAP-51 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Own texture conversion and naming.** Every material with an `{"own": "<png>"}` texture is read from the project folder, decoded to RGBA8 and written as a one-level 32-bit DTX (`dc_tex::write_bgra8`, uncompressed, 1..65535 on a side) at the PNG's project path with the extension replaced by `.dtx`, under `assets/` (a path outside `assets/` is placed under it; the extension rule is MAP-45's `dtx_rel_path`): `assets/ground.png` -> `assets/ground.dtx`, which is the name the build writes into the texture tables as `@mod:<id>/assets/ground.dtx`. Two materials naming one PNG share one DTX; a missing PNG is `texture.missing`, an unreadable one `texture.format` (both refuse the export). Pictures the project ships under `assets/pictures/` are converted the same way. | one-level BGRA8 | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.2 size rule "own textures count w*h*4", 6.3) | none | `dc_mapkit::export::{dtx_path_of, png_to_dtx}`; test `export::tests::helpers` |
| MAP-52 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Screenshot and radar on the software path.** `export` parses the built `.dat` back and renders it with the CPU rasteriser (MAP-53), never a GPU: the radar `assets/pictures/<key>_radar.dtx` is the `top` view at 256 x 256 (orthographic, +x right, +z up, the geometry extent fitted with a 4 % margin, aspect kept), and the record's `radar.min` / `radar.max` are the world x / z of the picture's left-bottom and right-top edges (`top_bounds`), so a reader maps a world point to the picture linearly; the screenshot `screenshots/main.png` is the `iso` view at 640 x 480 (under the 1 MiB screenshot cap). ## Community map builder, stage 2: the AI-native surface (mapkit-stage2 ai slice, 2026-11-01)

Branch `mapkit-stage2` ai slice (docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md section 7, D8: `dc-mapkit run` Lua generators, `dc-mapkit mcp`, the playbook v2, the `mapkit` skill, the example generators). Our own tool (no 2009 counterpart); ids MAP-56 .. MAP-60. Amends MAP-11 in one point: a solid whose material carries the sky flag is not a floor for `ground: true` (the stage-1 templates had grounded every spawn on the sky lid at y 744; `ops::is_floor`).

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAP-56 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The Lua `map` API and batch semantics.** `dc-mapkit run <dir> <script.lua\|-> [--budget N] [--dry-run]` runs the script in the mod sandbox (`dc_mod_lua::LuaSandbox`: Lua 5.4 text chunks; `string`, `table`, `math`, `utf8`; no `os`, `io`, `debug`, `package`, `load`; `require` has no root and refuses) with one extra global `map`. Every mutating call builds exactly one `Op` (`map.add{}` -> `add`, `map.remove`, `map.move(id, pos \| {delta} \| {ground})`, `map.set`, `map.rename`, `map.solid.box{} / wedge / cylinder{sides} / prism{points}` -> `solid.add`, `map.solid.set`, `map.prefab(name, {})`, `map.import{}`, `map.material.set{}` (a text `texture` is an own PNG path), `map.terrain.gen{} / noise{}` -> `terrain.gen`, `raise`, `lower`, `smooth`, `flatten`), applies it to a WORKING COPY (so an invalid op fails at its line and later queries see the pending state) and queues it; when the script ends the queue is applied to the real project as ONE batch through `ops::apply` (all-or-nothing), with one history snapshot before the write (`run` label); a script that errors (syntax, runtime, budget, a refused op outside `pcall`) changes nothing; a refused call inside `pcall` queues nothing and the script goes on. Queries (`map.query{class, id, near}` -> plain tables `{id, class, name, pos, rot, props}`, `near` as the positional `{x, z, r}` or the named `{x =, z =, r =}` (the MCP `get` tool's form; any other key or a missing one is refused with both spellings in the message), `map.solids{group, brush}`, `map.info()`, `map.ops()`, `map.terrain.height(x, z)`, `map.ground(x, z)`) read the working copy. Arguments: vec3 as `{x, y, z}` or `{x =, y =, z =}`; property values text / number / bool / vec3 / `{rgb = {r, g, b}}`; `rot` is the short name of `rot_y_deg` on solids (a table carrying both is refused, nothing is dropped silently); a missing optional field takes the op's default; an UNKNOWN field name is an error (the message lists the op's fields); calls work with `.` or `:`. Constants `map.MODES`, `map.CLASSES`, `map.BRUSHES`, `map.PRESETS`, `map.FALLOFFS`, `map.seed` (the project's seed). DETERMINISM: `math.random` is replaced in the generator's environment by a host function over a splitmix64 state seeded from the project's `seed` (the same step `ops::noise` uses; fresh per run) with Lua's call forms (no argument: a float in [0, 1) from the top 53 bits; `(m)`: an integer in 1..m; `(m, n)`: in m..n; an empty interval, a bound without an integer representation or more than two arguments is an error as in Lua), and `math.randomseed` stays out of the sandbox, so the same project and script queue the same ops on every run and `--dry-run` previews exactly what `run` writes. `print` lines are collected (`result.prints`, stderr `script: ...`). Diagnostics: `script.error` with path `script:<line>` for a syntax or runtime error; a refused op keeps its own code with path `script:<line>.<field>`; the CLI answer is the `apply` shape plus `ops` and `prints`. | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md section 7 `run`) | `--budget`, `--dry-run` | `dc_mapkit::script::{generate, run, Generated, RunOptions}`, `cli::run_script`; tests `script::tests::*` (batch, pending queries, line + code of a refusal, pcall, budget, syntax line, sandbox has no os / io / load, colon calls, the three example generators validate and are deterministic, `math_random_is_seeded_from_the_project_and_keeps_luas_call_forms`, `query_near_takes_both_forms_and_rot_next_to_rot_y_deg_is_refused`) |
| MAP-57 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Generator budget.** A generator gets 1,000,000,000 Lua instructions (`script::DEFAULT_BUDGET`, `SandboxLimits::with_instruction_limit`; the mod default of 10 M stops a per-cell loop over a 512 x 512 grid) and otherwise the sandbox defaults (64 MiB heap, 200 frames, 4 MiB strings, 1000 print lines); `--budget N` (N >= 1) overrides it per run; an exhausted budget is the diagnostic `script.budget` (path `script`, fix hint: raise the budget or use the bulk terrain ops). The bulk ops exist so a script rarely loops per cell: `terrain.gen` / `smooth` / `raise` / `lower` / `flatten` touch the whole grid or a circle in one call. | 1e9 | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md section 7 `--budget`) | `--budget` | `dc_mapkit::script::DEFAULT_BUDGET`; test `script::tests::the_budget_stops_a_runaway_loop_and_syntax_errors_carry_the_line` |
| MAP-58 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **MCP protocol minimum and transport.** `dc-mapkit mcp` is JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio with serde_json only: one UTF-8 JSON object per line, no embedded newlines; ALL logging on stderr (the verbs run in-process through `cli::run_cli` with stdout captured into the tool result and stderr forwarded); works without a ROM or GPU. The `mcp` verb is served by `run_cli` BEFORE the envelope printer: stdout carries response lines and nothing else (no empty line or `{verb: "mcp"}` envelope after the session, `--json` or not), the verb exits 0 when stdin closes and 1 with the failure on stderr when a stream breaks; lines are read as bytes (`read_until`) and decoded lossily, so a line that is not UTF-8 is answered `-32700` like any non-JSON line and the session goes on. `initialize` answers `{protocolVersion: <the client's when it is 2025-06-18 or 2024-11-05, else "2025-06-18"; 2025-03-26 is NOT echoed because that revision requires JSON-RPC batch support and a top-level array is `-32600` here>, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}, resources: {subscribe: false, listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: "dc-mapkit", version}, instructions}` (no `prompts`); `notifications/initialized`, `notifications/cancelled` and every other notification (no `id`) are accepted silently and never answered; `ping` -> `{}`; `tools/list` -> `{tools: [{name, description, inputSchema}]}` (JSON Schema objects, `additionalProperties: false`); `tools/call` -> `{content: [{type: "text", text: <the CLI JSON envelope>}, ...], isError}` where a verb failure (CLI exit 1 / 2, a refused batch, a missing required argument) is `isError: true`, never a JSON-RPC error; an unknown tool name or a non-object `arguments` / `params` is `-32602`; `resources/list` / `resources/read` serve `mapkit://playbook` (docs/MAPKIT_AGENTS.md, embedded), `mapkit://schema` (the schema JSON) and `mapkit://vocab` (docs/MAPKIT_VOCAB.md) as `{contents: [{uri, mimeType, text}]}`, an unknown uri is `-32002`; unknown method `-32601`; a line that is not JSON `-32700` (id null); a JSON value that is not a 2.0 request object `-32600`. `render` adds `{type: "image", data: <base64 PNG>, mimeType: "image/png"}` content (own RFC 4648 encoder, no dependency). | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md section 7 MCP bullet as amended by the plan review item 13) | none | `dc_mapkit::mcp::{serve, serve_verb, Server, tools, call_tool, PROTOCOL_VERSION, SUPPORTED_VERSIONS}`, `cli::run_cli_with_stdin`; conformance test `mcp::tests::a_scripted_client_runs_the_handshake_and_every_tool` (in-memory pipes: handshake, the two echoed versions, 2025-03-26 answered with ours, the batch array, every error code, every tool against a temp project), `mcp::tests::the_mcp_verb_writes_only_response_lines_and_survives_a_non_utf8_line` |
| MAP-59 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The tool list and the project-path rule.** Tools, in listing order: `new`, `info`, `validate`, `build`, `export`, `render`, `apply` (`ops` array + `dry_run`), `get` (`class`, `id`, `near: {x, z, r}`), `terrain` (`op` + the flat flags of the CLI verb + `dry_run`), `snapshot`, `history`, `revert`, `run` (`script` = inline Lua text, `budget`, `dry_run`), `rom_list` (`kind`, `filter`, `thumbs`, `rom`), `schema` (`ops`), plus the flat typed twins `add_object` (`add`), `move_object` (`move`), `set_property` (`set`), `remove_object` (`remove`), `terrain_noise` (`terrain.gen`) whose input schemas are GENERATED from `schema::OPS` (field type text -> JSON Schema; the required set = the fields the example op refuses to deserialise without) plus `dry_run`; each twin is a one-op batch through the same `apply` path (snapshot + save). Every tool takes `project` (the project folder, absolute or relative to the server's working directory; required on every tool except `schema` and `rom_list`, which accept and ignore it); a missing `project` answers `isError` with a usage text. The verb tools map 1:1 onto the CLI verbs and answer the CLI's `--json` envelope `{ok, verb, result, diagnostics}` as their text content; `render` runs the software path in-process exactly as the CLI arm does (the level plus the project's object markers, `render_report`; arguments `view`, `width`, `height`, `labels`, `grid`, `grid_step`, optional `out` file, else the CLI's default `<project>/build/render/<view>.png`) and answers the CLI's result (`view`, `image`, `width`, `height`, `triangles`, `legend`, `markers`, `grid_step`, `top_bounds`, plus `out` when given) with the PNG as image content. | MAP-60 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Skill and playbook.** `docs/MAPKIT_AGENTS.md` v2 is the one agent playbook (the loop, every verb with an example and its result shape, the ops reference, the vocabulary pointer to docs/MAPKIT_VOCAB.md, the Lua API reference, the MCP tool list and setup snippets for Claude Code `.mcp.json` and other stdio clients, limits, troubleshooting) and is embedded into the binary as the MCP resource `mapkit://playbook` (`include_str!`), so a served copy never drifts from the checkout that built it. Branch `mapkit-stage3` gui slice (docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md P3, D7 as amended by the plan review, 5.2 `gui`): the eframe / egui editor in `crates/dc-mapkit/src/gui/` and the second binary `dc-mapkit-gui`. Our own tool (no 2009 counterpart); ids MAP-61 .. MAP-66. Amends MAP-11 in one point: two more ops, `settings.set` (the world settings the build turns into `dc.world_settings`, `dc.global_light` and the sky model) and `meta.set` (the map's label and the mod metadata), so the GUI's world and metadata panels have an op to go through.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

While a drag or stroke is in progress the GUI previews on an in-memory copy and restores the pre-gesture state before committing the batch, so the result equals the batch applied by `dc-mapkit apply`. Undo / Redo are `history::revert` of the entry the gesture took (the revert's own `before revert` snapshot becomes the redo target); the history keeps 50 entries (MAP-14). ## Community map builder, stage 3: `play`, the starter map example and the vanilla++ proof (mapkit-stage3 play, 2026-11-01)

Branch `mapkit-stage3` play slice (docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md D9, 5.2 `play`, 6.3 examples, P5 vanilla++). Our own tool and our own test set-up (no 2009 counterpart); ids MAP-67 .. MAP-72. Found while running it: the scripted menu player (`--menu-pilot` / headless `--menu lobby`) never reached a modded lobby's match, because the mod consent prompt (CLI-1618) is the login screen's own window, which the pilot did not see, and `--pilot-map <n>` refused a number past the ROM's rows; both are amended below (MAP-69). Amended by mapkit-stage4 (project decision: community maps ride the Vanilla++ featured entry of the vanilla lobby): `play` runs that entry by default and keeps the stage-3 shape behind `--modded` (MAP-89), the recipe needs no second instance (MAP-71), the starter map has a review row (MAP-90).

| MAP-92 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **`rises` on a wedge.** `solid.add` and `solid.set` take `rises` (`north` +z, `east` +x, `south` -z, `west` -x), which sets the yaw; `size` stays `[width across, height, run along the slope]`. It is refused on a solid that is not a wedge and next to a rotation. The stored form stays `rot_y_deg`. No check can tell a sideways ramp from a meant one, so the fix is an unambiguous way to say it. |
| MAP-93 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Flat terrain.** `terrain.gen` takes the preset `flat`, and an amplitude of 0 means the same: one level floor at `base`. A new terrain then keeps the default height range (amplitude 256) so the brushes can still raise and lower it. |
| MAP-94 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **Running a generator again.** The op `clear` and `map.clear` remove everything placed, or the solids of one `group` and the objects of one `class`; materials, terrain, settings, metadata and asset files stay. A clear that empties the project resets `next_id`, so the same generator gets the same ids; this is the one case where an id comes back. Exact repeats of a solid or object are the warnings `solid.duplicate` and `object.duplicate`, one diagnostic per kind. |
| MAP-95 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **`render --textured`.** The flat view stays the default because it needs no GPU, binaries or ROM. `--textured` writes the current build, exports it and runs a headless `dc-client`, keeping the last of 3 frames as `build/render/<view>_textured.png`. Two new client flags serve it: `--camera X,Y,Z,YAW,PITCH` (degrees, positive pitch down; the match still runs from the spawn) and `--clean-frame` (no HUD, no debug panel). `top` and `iso` place the camera outside the world, framed from the world's box. |
| MAP-96 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The sky is not lit.** Sky model faces get the neutral vertex colour 0x80 instead of baked light: baking shaded each side of the box by the sun, and its edges showed as a dark rectangle in the sky. Flat view materials past the 8 of the palette get their own hue instead of wrapping, which hid a ninth material against the first. |
| MAP-97 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **`fit` on a material.** `[u0, v0, u1, v1]` (0..1, v down) maps that part of the texture once across each face of a solid, unmirrored from outside; u follows the solid's local +x on a top or bottom face, and runs the other way on a sky model, which is seen from inside. Solids only. Without it a material tiles by its `tile`, which cuts any texture that pictures one object or holds an atlas. |
| MAP-98 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **`map.settings` in Lua.** A generator sets fog, sun, ambient and sky through the same fields as the `settings.set` op. A generator that builds a whole mood could not reach them before. |
| MAP-99 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **A tiled texture turns with its solid.** On a solid with a yaw, a tiling material projects along the solid's own axes, anchored at its centre, not along the world's: the world projection lay slanted across a turned floor and squeezed its sides. An unturned solid keeps the world projection, so its bytes do not change. |
| MAP-100 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; project decision) | **A reviewed pack may name ROM textures.** The owner approved Shipping Container, whose surfaces are ROM texture paths resolved from each player's own ROM. The zip holds paths and no ROM data, and it lives in the lobby's mods folder, never in the tree. Its project source stays out of this repository (CLEANROOM.md section 4), so the row's `source_repo` names the project and `reviewer_note` says where the source is. |
| MAP-100a (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; project decision) | **A map's preview and loading pictures.** A map needs both when it is published. `dc-mapkit pictures` draws them with the game's renderer: the preview at 256 x 256, the size of the ROM's waiting room map pictures, drawn 3 times larger and scaled down; the loading picture at 1024 x 768, the page the client stretches it over (MAP-32). `export` warns with `picture.missing` when one is absent and still exports. On a map using ROM textures these pictures show them, so they stay in the project and the pack, out of the tree. |
| MAP-101 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-02) | **The end camera of a community map.** A ROM world cuts to an overview at the round result through a camera object and trigger scripts (DSV-112), which the vocabulary does not offer, so a community map kept the player's own view and gun. The class `dc.end_camera` (a point: `pos` the place, `rot` x looks down, `rot` y turns) becomes a world camera without a script: live at the round result, off at the next round's start, movement held, the same create and change records as DSV-113, so the client needs no change. `build` adds an overview over the south edge of the spawns' area, under the top of the world, when a project places none. A cut, not a move: the ROM's moving shots on bomb maps are not modelled. |
| MAP-102 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-02) | **A community room borrows rules from the default ROM map, not its name.** The room line of a community map still takes the mode row's keys from the mode's default ROM map (MAP-37), but `obj` (the banner's title image, which showed that ROM map's name at load-in) and `large` (its large map) stay out. `obj` becomes the pack's `assets/pictures/<world stem>_title.dtx` when the file is there, by convention rather than a record field, so a client that does not know the convention still loads the pack; without one the banner shows only the mode text. `dc-mapkit pictures` draws the title (512 x 128, the ROM banner size) from the project's name, in Roboto. |
| MAP-103 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER DECISION 2026-11-02) | **A map on ROM textures ships plain pictures.** A render of ROM textures holds ROM pixels, which a pack may not carry (MODDING_GUIDE section 8), so `dc-mapkit pictures` writes a name card for the preview and the loading screen of any project with a ROM material, and renders only a project of own textures. `render --textured` still draws anything locally, for the author to look at. Amends MAP-100a, and supersedes the note of MAP-100 on Shipping Container's pictures. |
| MAP-104 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03) | **Outside models in a map.** `dc-mapkit asset` converts a glTF binary (`meshopt-rs` for its compression, WebP textures through `image`) into OBJ + PNG per material, removing triangles none of 26 rays from their centre can leave through, and simplifying with a relative error of at most 0.035 (a model keeps more triangles than asked rather than lose its look; only one over 4 times its budget takes the sloppy pass). An OBJ's `vt` and `vn` now survive: a model's polygons keep exact corner texture coordinates and corner normals in the render data. A material flag `hidden` makes a solid collision only, never drawn. The level's collision model now holds only what can be hit (solid polygons, hidden cores, sky faces): a see-through model costs it nothing and no longer runs the tree out of its budget. Render vertices equal in position, colour and rounded uv and normal are shared, in every map: the test map's world file fell from 9.2 to 3.5 MB; `size.estimate` counts 70 bytes per see-through triangle. `bake.shadow` (`settings.set` `bake_shadow`, default 0, off) darkens floor and wall corners from five rays to the sun and eight low contact rays against solids and hidden cores, not a model's own corners. |
| MAP-105 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-03 "items like banana can be clipped through") | **A placed model is solid by default.** `dc-mapkit asset` records the model's convex outline from above (at most 10 corners, grown past the model: amended by MAP-111) and `asset.place` adds a hidden prism of that outline at 101 % of the model's height, in a material `core_<surface>`; `solid: false` leaves it out, `surface` names the surface id. It is a block: nothing passes under a forklift's forks or through a rack. A texture within 10 per channel of one colour is written 4 x 4, and a picture byte-equal to one in the project reuses that file, so a many-part model costs a fraction of its textures. |
| MAP-106 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-03 "a lot of broken textures") | **Converting without breaking textures.** The vertex-clustering pass ignores texture seams and was what smeared crates and bent drums, so a textured part never takes it. `asset --proxy box\|round` replaces a model by a box or a prism of up to 12 sides: each face gets the full-detail source drawn straight on (3 x 3 samples per pixel, nearest surface wins, uncovered pixels take a neighbour's colour; a face that sees nothing takes the model's mean). `--strict` now tries a relative error up to 0.1; a part still over twice its share becomes its area-weighted average colour and only then may take the vertex-clustering pass. A simplification welds by position and texture coordinate, not by normal, and normals are recomputed per corner afterwards: faces share a normal up to about 42 degrees. Separate pieces under 2 % of the model's diagonal are dropped. `KHR_texture_transform` and `COLOR_0` are read (the SimReady models tried have white vertex colours). A double-sided part with over 5 % open edges gets its back faces, as the game draws one side only. |
| MAP-107 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 "a lot of the models still need work", "better wall / floor textures") | **Rebaked models and better textures.** `asset --proxy rebake` simplifies a model by shape alone (texture seams released), groups its faces into charts that turn under 45 degrees from their largest face, packs them on one new texture and draws each texel from the full-detail source along the face's normal: the source's colour with its normal map drawn in (`1 + 0.55 (0.6 nx + 0.8 ny)`), its fine shape against a fixed light (0.6 .. 1.25) and contact shading from 12 rays (up to 65 % darker). `--two-sided` adds back faces. `--leave-out` drops parts by words of their material names, for wire mesh, as this renderer has no cut-outs and a bake would turn it into a solid sheet. `asset --relief k` multiplies a texture by `1 + k (0.6 nx + 0.8 ny)` from its normal map, as this renderer has none. Export writes an opaque power-of-two texture as DXT1 with mips down to a side of 4, and resizes any other opaque picture of at least 256 x 256 to powers of two, as a loading picture is stretched when drawn. |
| MAP-108 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 "better lighting variation") | **Lightmaps.** `bake.lightmap` (`settings.set` `bake_lightmap`, units a texel, 0 is off) bakes the map's flat surfaces onto 256 x 256 pages: tiles of at most 200 texels, sections as in RENDER_2009.md 5.2 (kind 2 with the page, kind 4 with the texture, same triangles), texels packed as in 6.1. A texel adds each `dc.point_light` (fade `(1 - d^2 / r^2)^2`, four shadow samples over a 9 unit disc) and the sun (four samples, only where nothing blocks it up to 8,192 units), one bounce from 20 fixed rays (the light on what they hit times its material's average colour, hidden cores count as dim grey, a miss as sky), and the ambient light less up to 75 % where those rays hit within 110 units; the bounce and ambient are blurred over 5 x 5 texels. A byte is value x 128. A model's corners (kind 1) take the lamps and the sun with cores ignored, and 2.2 x the ambient light, as a rebaked texture has its contact shading and no bounce is gathered for a corner. The light grid (cells of 128 units) takes lamps and sun with a floor of ambient + 0.14, so a player stays visible in the dark. See-through solids' undersides and edges thinner than 3 units are not drawn in a lit map. |
| MAP-109 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-03 "forklifts can't be shot through even though you can see through them", models still broken) | **Rebake by sealed shell; collision that follows the model.** `--proxy rebake` no longer simplifies a model's own mesh, whose open edges and hidden parts break it: it marks the source's surfaces on a grid of 160 cells along the longest side, floods from outside, and takes the faces between what the flood reached and the rest as a closed surface, smoothed by six Taubin steps (0.5, -0.53) and moved in half a cell. That simplifies with a relative error up to 0.12. Texels sample the source along the normal from 4 cells out. The same grid at about 40 cells gives `hull_boxes`: a coarse cell is solid when a tenth of it is, so a thin bar across two cells stays, merged greedily, at most 40 boxes a model (a coarser grid when more). A model solid over 40 % of its bounds, or under 1 m long, gets none. `asset.place` uses them as the hidden core, turned with the model; models without them keep the footprint prism of MAP-105. `build` warns (`face.overlap`) when two drawn faces lie within 1 unit on the same side, the cause of flickering. |
| MAP-110 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 "could we add some cool graffiti") | **Paint on walls.** `asset` takes a PNG with power-of-two sides and makes a flat sheet `--width` metres wide, cut into cells of at most 0.5 m as a model is lit at its corners. A material texture with texels of alpha under 128 is exported as DXT1 with holes and the command `AlphaRef 128`, read by clients as they are (RENDER_2009.md 10.3); opaque textures are unchanged. A model part whose material has holes takes the light of the surface up to 12 units behind each corner. The build warns (`paint.off_wall`) when a corner has no such surface or another one within 1 unit in front. The build warns of coplanar overlapping faces of one material too when the map has lightmaps, as their light differs. A model given 6,000 triangles or more is rebaked on a shell of 256 cells instead of 160. |
| MAP-111 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-03 "many of the objects in the game and walls don't have bullet impact marks") | **Bullet marks show.** A mark lands on the collision surface and is drawn at that depth (cshell+0x2c8dda), so a hidden core inside its model or paint in front of a wall hid it. A footprint now grows until it holds every point of the model, then 1 % more (`glb::CORE_MARGIN`), and the prism is 101 % of the height. A material flagged `skin` with `hidden` is collision that casts no shadow and bounces no light, for a thin layer over paint. A model over 1 m takes collision boxes instead of the prism unless it is under 0.5 m tall or fills at least 60 % of that prism and 40 % of its bounds, as the prism would fill the air over a low part (a bench); up to 80 boxes, a coarse cell solid from one part in 16. `rom surfaces` lists `marks`: whether the row shows marks and has a hole sprite, read from the ROM at run time. |
| MAP-112 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 trying a Vanilla++ pack on a map) | **`dc-mapkit play --with-mod <folder>`.** Other mods go into the set of the local server beside the map, validated and packed as `dc-modkit pack` does. Local play only. `--loadout <slot>:<item>,...` sets what a new character starts with there, to try a gun. `--inventory <item>,...` puts items in its inventory, not equipped (CD-99). |
| MAP-113 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REPORT 2026-11-04 "There's no bombsites on either shipping container or freight hall, somehow the bots can plant but I don't even get a bomb in my inventory") | **A community map's bomb sites work like a ROM world's, with nothing for the mapper to place.** (a) The bomb item: a community map has no GMS row, so `find_gms` found none and no attacker got the item (bots still planted, with the use hold, DSV-240). A world with a `dc.player_spawn` now takes the first GMS row of the room's mode, which names the same weapon row on all 6 ROM Search and Destroy worlds. (b) The site markers: a ROM world places them by hand and its triggers and planted commands switch them; the vocabulary has neither. In a class 2 / 3 room the server gives each `dc.bomb_site` a looping live marker, on from the start, and a planted marker, off until a plant, at the site's centre, 16 units above the floor found straight down from there (else the box bottom), laid flat, using the two effect groups the ROM indicators use (found at run time by pinned key). A plant switches every live marker off and its own site's planted marker on; the next round restores them (CLI-1340). Other modes show none. A server without those groups draws none. The site still is the box, the marker does not grow with `extent`. | 16 units; rotation as ROM | OBSERVED: ROM world indicators (9 to 16 units above the floor, the same flat rotation, looped), ROM GMS rows; the markers and the fallback row are ours; tests `game::bomb::tests`, `world_objects_rom rom_a_community_map_takes_the_modes_bomb_item`, `bomblook the_rom_has_the_bomb_model_and_both_groups`; played: client and bot on Freight Hall (attacker spawns moved in a scratch copy): key 6 draws the bomb, green ring, plant, red ring, timer | none | `bomblook::{SITE_LIVE_FX, SITE_PLANTED_FX}`, `game::bomb::add_site_markers`, `coop_rom::first_mode_gms`, `Session::plan_world_objects` |

| MAP-115 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER REQUEST 2026-11-04 "should have a circle around it on the ground too") | **A community map's capture flags have the ROM's ground ring.** In a class 7 / 8 room the server gives each `dc.capture_flag` with team 1 or 2 a looping flat effect at the flag's x and z, 16 units above the floor below it, always on and also while the flag is away, using the group a ROM world places under that team's flag (found at run time by pinned key). ROM worlds are unchanged; a server without those groups draws none.
