| VAR-1 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER DECISION 2026-11-02) | **A weapon variant is its own row.** Item numbers 500..899 are for variants, and 900..999 stay for new guns (the ROM's rows stop below 500, and numbers from 1000 mean other item types). A row with `variant_of = <base>` is built from the finished base row when the content is applied, on the lobby, the game server and the client alike. Type, slot and socket lookups, the shop and storage rows, the HUD's kill-feed images, the first-person model, sounds and muzzle effects go through the base gun. A variant carries its base gun's name but takes no entry in the command table built from `[WeaponOrder]`: that table stays as the ROM has it, and a variant uses its base gun's switch command and class. Gun game keeps to ROM rows, so a variant does not join its ladder. See docs/GUNKIT_PLAN.md. |
| VAR-2 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER DECISION 2026-11-02) | **A variant only changes how a gun looks.** Besides `variant_of` it may set only cosmetic keys, and the content document refuses any other key, so a variant and its base gun play the same. Other players see the base gun's third-person model with the `HHSkin<k>` the variant sets. |
| VAR-3 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER DECISION 2026-11-02) | **A camo ships as a pattern and a recipe.** A pack may not carry ROM pixels (MODDING_GUIDE section 8; the rule is taken from gen1recomp's design, not its code), so a skin names `@camo:paint:<base row>:<skin key>:[keep=x,y,radius[/x,y,radius...]:]<pattern>`, and the client paints it in memory from the player's own texture and the pack's pattern. Each texel is the pattern's colour times the base's brightness over the mean brightness of the base's drawn texels (luma above 0.04), limited to 0.3..1.5, with the base's alpha. The pattern repeats twice across the base's width at any texture size, averaged when the base is smaller. `keep` circles, in texels of the base texture, stay as the base drew them with a 2-texel soft edge, so a camo leaves a scope's lens alone. The shop's pictures of a variant are painted the same way, from the ROM's picture of its base gun, unless the variant names its own icon. The game server announces a path starting with `@` exactly as written, because the 2009 spelling (upper case, `\` separators) would break it. Our own values, tuned by eye on the G36E. |
| VAR-4 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER DECISION 2026-11-02) | **A camo may carry one light effect.** A `@camo:` path may add `fx=<drift u>,<drift v>,<lowest gain>,<highest gain>,<seconds per pulse>`: the pack's pattern is added over the gun as light after the render style's stages, repeating as the paint does, drifting by the given repeats per second, with the gain swinging between the two values (0 seconds: steady at the highest). `<painted pattern>|<effect pattern>` gives the effect a pattern of its own, so that what moves is not also painted still underneath; a still shop picture then uses the effect's pattern. A mask made at load keeps it off the base's unused space and its `keep` circles. Limits so that nothing strobes or blinds: a pulse takes at least 1 second, the gain stays within 0..1, and the drift within 1 repeat per second. Only a model with an effect reads the clock or writes its uniforms for it, so other models cost what they did. A fixed effect, not scripting. Whether a look makes a player too easy to see stays a review call (docs/GUNKIT_PLAN.md D5). The 2009 renderer has no such effect; these are our own values. |
| VAR-5 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT; USER DECISION 2026-11-02) | **A variant may wear another row's models.** `variant_look_of = <row>` takes that row's first-person and third-person models, skins, render styles and first-person position (`Pos`) and nothing else. The other row's sounds, sound radius, ammunition and muzzle effects stay out, because a row with a similar look can play differently: the ROM's ghillie L96A1 is heard from less far. So that variant looks suppressed and is heard as far as the plain gun. A pack ships the row number and no ROM path or file. The menus show the other row's pictures. The two rows' clips must match in length, which is checked by hand so far (`dc-gunkit` should check it): the client's weapon timing follows the drawn model's clips. A character whose hand identifier has no model in that row draws no first-person gun, as it would for that row itself. |

## Community map builder, stage 3: CI and release packaging (mapkit-stage3 release, 2026-11-01)

Branch `mapkit-stage3` release slice (docs/MAPKIT_PLAN.md 6.6, P5; the review items on Windows play and GitHub Releases). Our own tool (no 2009 counterpart); ids MAP-73 .. MAP-76, packaging rules only. Code: `tools/mapkit_pack_mac.sh`, `tools/mapkit_pack_win.py`, `.github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml`.

| Id | Rule | Default | Evidence | Config key | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MAP-73 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The macOS MapKit package.** `tools/mapkit_pack_mac.sh [--bin-dir DIR] [--x86-dir DIR] [--out DIR] [--name NAME]` writes `out_mapkit/<name>.zip` (name `DeCombat-MapKit-mac-<commit>`; `out_mapkit/` is ignored by git) holding `<name>/DeCombat MapKit.app` and `<name>/README.md`. The bundle: `CFBundleIdentifier` `org.decombat.mapkit`, `CFBundleName` / `CFBundleDisplayName` "DeCombat MapKit", `CFBundleVersion` = the commit, `LSMinimumSystemVersion` 12.0, `NSHighResolutionCapable`, category developer-tools, `CFBundleExecutable` = the GUI binary `dc-mapkit-gui` DIRECTLY (no launcher script: LaunchServices starts it with no arguments; the ROM comes from the tool's own discovery rule MAP-54 and the GUI's banner), the console `dc-mapkit` and the three game binaries `dc-lobby-server`, `dc-dserver`, `dc-client` beside it in `Contents/MacOS` (the folder `dc-mapkit play` searches first), the icon `Contents/Resources/mapkit.icns` rendered from `assets/icon/mapkit_logo.png` at 16..512 px plus @2x through sips / iconutil (the friend package's pipeline). Binaries come from `--bin-dir` (default `target/release`, else `target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release`); each one with a twin in `--x86-dir` (default `target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release`) is joined by `lipo` into one universal binary; every binary is signed ad hoc AFTER lipo (the linker's arm64 signature does not survive it) and the bundle once more with `--deep`. A missing `dc-mapkit-gui` makes the console `dc-mapkit` the executable with a warning (so the packer runs before the GUI slice lands and on a debug build, `--bin-dir target/debug`); a missing game binary is an error (exit 2). The README carries the first-run notes: "Open Anyway" (or `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`), choosing the ROM folder (remembered in `<profile>/mapkit.toml`), the console path inside the bundle for `PATH` / `.mcp.json`, the build commit and the architectures. Nothing of the game and nothing of the building machine goes in. | as stated | ours (MAPKIT_PLAN.md 5.2 "On Windows `gui` is a second thin binary ... the one the .app and the zip put in front", 6.6; friend_pack_mac.sh) | `--bin-dir`, `--x86-dir`, `--out`, `--name` | `tools/mapkit_pack_mac.sh`; checked by hand on a debug build (bundle signed ad hoc, plist lints, the console binary runs from inside the bundle) |

Branch `mapkit-stage4` lobby and host slice (project decision: community maps ride the Vanilla++ entry's curated set). Our own feature, no 2009 counterpart; ids MAP-80 .. MAP-84. The modded-lobby path (MAP-35 .. MAP-39) stays as it is.

A record is an object with every field of `dc_mod_lua::MapRecord` under its own name: `mod_id`, `patched_by`, `id`, `name`, `description`, `world`, `modes`, `goals` as `[[mode, goal], ...]`, `round_seconds`, `picture`, `loading`, `radar` as `{picture, min: [x, z], max: [x, z]}`, `players` as `{min, max}`; an unset field is `null`, never missing. | MAP-82 (proposed; DC-DEFAULT) | **The map table belongs to the entry.** `Core::maps_for(Some(entry))` is the ROM rows plus that entry's maps when it has a curated set, else the lobby-wide table; `maps_for(None)` is the lobby-wide one, and curated sets exist only on a vanilla lobby (LG-313), whose lobby-wide table has no community row. Every room query goes through `Core::maps_of_channel` (create, pick, mode change, launch, room line, reward factors). ## NX rewards (branch nx-rewards, USER REQUEST 2026-11-01)

Our own economy rules, also on vanilla instances; no 2009 evidence (the 2009 client only shows and spends the balance). Numbers from the ROM shop list: a 7-day NX gun 2900, 30 days 5900-6900, 90 days 9900-11900, permanent 24900-29900. Rewards go to the prepaid balance (the purchase dialogs default to it and it has no rank requirement, CD-37, CLI-774). Each instance pays in its own DB, so a modded instance pays in its own ledger only.

| id | rule | default | evidence | config key | hook |

No bots: names ending in `bot<digits>` (LG-260) and `--test-bot-account`s. The box "Daily bonus: +N NX" uses the notice path (0x303 +0x104 -> 0x366 / 0x367, CD-73); the login's own 0x344 / 0x345 carries the balance, so the frames of a login do not change. | on, 250 NX: 30-day gun in 24-28 days, 7-day gun in 12 | SPEC PROTOCOL_2009.md 0x303 +0x104, 0x345, 0x367 | `rewards.nx_enabled`, `rewards.nx_daily` | none |

A pick or a move of such an entry whose claim does not name it or differs (or is absent: the 2009 client, an older DeCombat client) gets **0x3f12** (`+6 u32 entry id`, line with the text for the player) then the refused 0x20b / 0x3b3, and a log line `client <addr>: entry <id> mod set mismatch`; a claim counts for one pick. Its channels refuse a session that did not pick it (a `--lenient` login). A pick of any other entry looks at nothing: a lobby without a set sends no new frame, and with one the login's frames differ only by 0x3f10. The entry's weapon content goes to that entry's game servers alone (`-content` from `<data>/entry_mods/<entry>/`; to a remote host in the `start` request, HOST_AGENT.md §3); its community maps are that entry's alone too (MAP-82 .. A login field of `;b=1` with no name takes the first free seat. A seat is in use while a connection is logged in on it and until the session key of its pick ends; nothing else holds it, so a crash frees it and a lobby restart frees all. At any count above 0 a person may enter a full room with a bot: a bot makes way first. The bot is chosen by not being the host, then the larger team, then the newest; a GM never leaves; clan rooms are left out. The room sees a plain leave (0x3034 reason 0), the bot alone a removal (reason 1), and it is not put on the room's kicked list. A hand-over goes to the longest-present person before any bot. dc-botclient reads its own removal: it leaves the match, passes over the room for 60 s when a person was there (20 s otherwise), and takes a refused entry as a 20 s pass-over instead of ending. |

| LG-326 (DC-DEFAULT: LG-326 proposed; launch security review) | **Connection caps and a time limit before the login.** At most 64 connections per source address on the lobby's TCP ports together (auth, lobby, clan, web) and 4000 in all; loopback is not counted. A connection that has not logged in within 120 s is closed; a logged-in one has no limit. A refused connection is closed at once and logged once per 10 s per port; a failed accept pauses 100 ms. The units' `LimitNOFILE` goes to 16384. Before this, one address could open sockets until the lobby ran out of descriptors or threads, and the accept loop then filled the log. |
| LG-321 (DC-DEFAULT: LG-321 proposed; launch security review) | **Clan pages of a public lobby only from the account's logged-in address.** The 2009 page URLs carry the login name and no secret, so `?p=<name>` was all it took to act as that online player (leave, kick, set the notice, disband). Two players behind one address can still act as each other: larger fix needs a secret in the URL, which only our client could send. |

Get the new version at <url>." and no login follows; below `latest` it says "A new DeCombat version (x) is available. Get it at <url>." once per run on the next screen and the login goes on. No answer, a broken document or any development build: nothing happens. |

| LG-327 (DC-DEFAULT: LG-327 proposed; project decision) | **Seat ticket.** The lobby makes 128 random bits per player and match, kept for a rejoin of that match, and sends them to the game server as the `ticket=<hex>` token of the `user` line (through a host agent unchanged) and to the player as our push 0x3f0c right before 0x3043. Our client appends `DCST` + the ticket after the 0x102 bytes of the hello blob. A roster name with a ticket is seated only with that ticket, compared in constant time; addresses are not compared. A missing or wrong one closes that link alone with the bye code of an unlisted name, the seated player is not touched, and the log takes the first 20 refusals of a match and then every hundredth. A hello with no ticket for a free seat also sends `@seat_refused <uid> noticket`, and the lobby sends that account one chat line per match saying its client is too old, at its first message back from the waiting room (a client drops what comes while its game screen is up). The connection's reader waits for its check, so its later messages stay behind the login. A check under way counts against the limits of LG-146 like a failure until it ends, so concurrent guesses cannot overrun ten per name or address. A full queue answers at once and counts nothing: login 0x201 reason 0x00030000, web 503. A password reset with a mailed code, an upgrade of an old row at the token endpoint and the operator's `account` commands still hash in place: they need a valid code, the right password or the console. |

| NET-10 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-10 proposed; project decision) | **Datagram cap.** No link datagram is larger than 548 UDP payload bytes (check byte included), a 576-byte IPv4 datagram: a reliable block is closed (and a longer message split with the 2009 `tail_cont`) so that it fits behind the largest ack, so its resends fit too; unreliable messages are packed only within the cap. An unreliable message longer than the cap alone still goes out by itself (the 2009 framing cannot split it) and is counted (`LinkStats::oversize_out`); none is longer today (the object stream is at most 4000 bits, DSV-17). Wire format unchanged: a 2009 peer reads smaller blocks as any other. | 548 B | measured on a headless 2 + 7 bot match: the 2009 budgets (8800-bit body) make server datagrams of up to 1101 B (preload and world-object runs, packed stream backlog of a waiting link); a path that drops datagrams over about 1070 B left a player stuck at the world load with only resends; with the cap the largest is 547 B and datagrams rise 1.5 % | none (`dc_net_engine::link::MAX_DATAGRAM_BYTES`) | `small_path::*`, `session_sim::nine_players_join_over_a_path_dropping_datagrams_over_{576,1200}_bytes` |
| NET-11 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-11 proposed; project decision) | **Unreliable data while reliable data waits.** Queued unreliable messages (the client's player updates, the server's object stream) keep going out while new reliable blocks are paused (more than 8 outstanding, a block resent more than twice, trickle mode); the 2009 pump sends no queued data at all while paused. | on | a waiting link stopped its player updates / object stream and then packed the backlog into full-size resends | none (`UNRELIABLE_WHILE_PAUSED`) | `small_path::unreliable_messages_flow_while_reliable_blocks_wait` |
| NET-12 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-12 proposed; project decision) | **Heartbeat bound.** The ack heartbeat interval is `min(max(200, L_ms), 1000)` ms. The 2009 `L_ms` grows with the time the side's own block has waited for an ack, so the heartbeat stopped exactly when the peer most needed acks; DSV-490's "a live client acks at least every 200 ms" holds again within 1 s. An extra ack is idempotent for a 2009 peer (DSV-4). | 1000 ms | as stated | none (`HEARTBEAT_MAX_MS`) | `small_path::the_heartbeat_ack_continues_while_waiting_for_an_ack` |

## World objects for players and bots (branch fix-world-0311, live report 2026-11-02 "WarHead: bots float near the sewer; a fence piece is missing at a spawn and walking through kills; Two Towers: bots walk on water"; proposed, project decision)

| DSV-500 (DC-DEFAULT: DSV-500 proposed; project decision) | **Message doors.** A rotating door of the world file that players do not open (not player-activated, locked in the file, or without a turn) is created like the other rotating doors (kind 2 named brush, DOOR-4), closed, and turns only by messages (`msg <door> on` / `off`, DSV-270); its activate entry is disabled (no use prompt). Before, such doors were not created at all, so the clients neither drew nor collided with them. Not in co-op rooms: their mission triggers that open these doors at run time are not run, and a door that never opens would block the mission. | on with `-doors on` | WarHead's TDM spawn fence: its gate is such a door, with a fall volume right behind it; only the quarantine mode's start trigger opens it (and switches that fall volume off). The gap killed whoever walked through. ROM survey: 4 worlds have such doors (WarHead 5, RapidStream 3 opened by some modes' start triggers, one unreferenced door on a co-op map, a co-op mission's 10) | `-doors` | `round2_sim::a_message_door_stands_closed_unless_the_start_scripts_open_it`, `rom_world::rom_warhead_spawn_gate_stands_closed_in_tdm_and_open_in_quarantine`, `rom_world::rom_garage_shutters_open_only_by_their_levers` |

| BOT-110 (DC-DEFAULT: BOT-110 proposed; project decision; replaces the bots' fixed file set) | **The bots collide with what the server creates.** A bot's collision set (its body, its line of sight, its grid) has the level model, the blocker polygons and the linked world models (doors and switches included) that the server created as named brushes with the solid flag 0x2000 (the client's rule CLI-230); a door or switch only while its object stands where it was created (closed). The set follows every change of the server's objects; a body standing on a model that left the set falls (CLI-1369). | row | rule | value | why | config | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLI-1840 (DC-DEFAULT: CLI-1840 proposed; USER REQUEST 2026-11-02) | **What a diagnostic report holds.** One `dcdiag1` JSON document, gzip, at most 1 MiB compressed (the largest file tail is halved until it fits): client version / commit / target, OS, CPU, cores, RAM, the window's GPU adapter and driver, the settings that matter, the match (lobby, entry, room, map, mode, how it ended), the link (totals: RTT, datagrams, resends, largest datagram; the overlay's last 5 s), the last connection test, the player's note (1000 characters), the login typed, and file tails: `dc-client.out` and `dc-client.prev.out` 256 KiB, `dc-client.net.jsonl` 512 KiB, its `.menu.jsonl` 128 KiB, `dc-client.watchdog.log` 64 KiB, `dc-client.hang.txt` and each stall / crash / panic text file 128 KiB. Minidumps never go. Every text is redacted first: values after password / token / secret / authorization keys (also in prose, "password is x"), `tok:` and `Bearer` values, `<20+>.<40+>` base64url token shapes, the cached token itself, mail addresses, the user and computer names at word boundaries (`%USER%`, `%HOST%`), every IPv4 / IPv6 address except loopback and the servers'. Ask: after the 2009 box of the failure a box Send report / Test connection / No (the test only for a lost link, a server bye, a failed join). Always: sent at once; after a network failure a box Test connection / OK, the result goes as a report of its own. Never: nothing is gathered. Sent whatever the consent: `/report [text]` (lobby or match chat), the bug form's "attach diagnostics" question (bug category). `/diag always|ask|never` changes it. Our own texts and button captions in the 2009 message box (three buttons centred, 10 px apart). | as stated | user request | `/diag`; `DC_DIAG=off` | `diag::{Consent, plan}`, `menu::diagbox`, `menu::popup::Popup::choice`; tests `diag::tests::the_plan_follows_the_consent`, `menu::diagbox::tests::our_three_button_box_lays_out_inside_the_message_box` |

## Network lab (branch netlab, 2026-11-03; proposed, project decision)

| row | rule | value | why | config | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NET-20 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-20 proposed; project decision) | **Impairment shim.** A test path around a client's UDP socket, in the process: per direction random loss, Gilbert-Elliott burst loss, latency with jitter (first in, first out), reordering, duplication, a datagram size limit, a packets-per-second policer, a bandwidth cap with a drop-tail queue; path-wide scheduled blackouts, NAT rebinding (a new source port), a NAT mapping that expires without sends, a middlebox that kills the flow after server silence. Seeded (a run repeats). `dc-botclient --net`, `dc-client --netlab` / `DC_NETLAB` (match socket only); off by default, nothing on the wire changes. | off | reproduce bad real-world paths (the 2026-11-02 campus drop) before players meet them, without admin rights or OS tools on any platform | `--net` / `--netlab` / `DC_NETLAB` | `dc_net_engine::impair` unit tests, `shim` tests |
| NET-21 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-21 proposed; project decision) | **Named paths.** `good`, `wifi`, `mobile_hotspot`, `australia`, `campus_firewall`, `cgnat_rebind`, `lossy_burst`, `blackout`, `clean` with the numbers in docs/NETLAB.md "Profiles"; `key=value` overrides. Our own estimates of typical paths, not measurements of any network. | docs/NETLAB.md | named, repeatable cases for a matrix and for a person's report | overrides | `impair::tests::every_profile_parses_and_clean_is_clean` |
| NET-22 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-22 proposed; project decision) | **Lab runner and thresholds.** `dc-netlab` runs matrices (`quick`, `soak`, `ci`, `campus`, custom `run --mix`) of 16-bot rooms on a local lobby + game server (ROM) or a game server on a synthetic world (no ROM, CI) and fails a bot on: an end other than its own quit / the normal close, no spawn or a slow one (20 s; 45 s impaired), a given-up reliable block, round trip median over `150 + 1.5 x path RTT + 2 x jitter + queues` (+200 ms bursty; p95: plus 1.5 s on a bursty path plus the longest blackout), fewer player updates counted by the server than the path delivers minus 5 points, a 10 s window under 5 datagrams from the client (not with blackouts), server resends over `5 % + 4 x downstream loss` (+10 % bursts, +2 x the blackout time share, +5 % policer / cap / size limit), 5 s windows without data at the bot beyond the blackouts, a server datagram over 548 B; a scenario also on more than 20 claimed hits with no kill (ROM runs). Update rates and gaps are reported, not judged (a dead player sends no updates; the bots' pace differs per platform) | as stated | first cut, tuned on the 2026-11-03 runs; the room is its own input baseline because the bots' pace differs per platform | `--xfail`, `--strict` | `dc-netlab` unit tests and lab runs |
| NET-23 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-23 proposed; project decision; amended by NET-24) | **A link follows its client to a new port.** A link datagram from an address without a link moves an open link of the same IP to it when that link has heard nothing for 250 ms and the datagram proves it belongs to that link: it carries the link's move secret (NET-24) and the sequence numbers it carries fit the link (cumulative ack within 64 of the link's newest block, reliable block within 64 of the next expected; a datagram with only unreliable data fits). The 2009 transport keys a link by address only, so a NAT that rebinds the client's port mid-match left both sides talking past each other until the silent drop (DSV-490): the server saw nothing from the old address, the client nothing from the server, exactly the shape of the 2026-11-02 report. First cut (2026-11-03) moved on sequence numbers alone; a review found that anyone behind the same public IP could guess them (about 64 datagrams) and take or close a seated player's link, so only our clients (they send the secret) move now; a 2009 client keeps working but is not followed. | 250 ms, window 64 | as stated | none (`ADDRESS_MOVE_SILENCE_MS`, `CLAIM_SEQ_WINDOW`) | `nat_rebind::*` (fails without the move), `session_sim::a_rebinding_player_keeps_the_seat_and_a_stranger_behind_the_same_nat_cannot_take_it`, the netlab `cgnat_rebind` bots |
| NET-24 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-24 proposed; project decision) | **The link move secret.** A game server that moves links (NET-23) gives each link a random 64-bit secret once, when its player enters the world (after the hello and its seat ticket, LG-327): reliable shell message `[13][0xf3][secret: 8 bytes]` (our shell id; a 2009 client drops it, GAME_MESSAGES_2009_S2C.md §7.2). Our client and dc-botclient then end every link datagram with a trailer: the body's framing closed explicitly (`has_unrel = 0`, or a zero-length unreliable entry; a bye also `has_rel = 0`), zero padding to a byte, `0xd3`, the 8 secret bytes, the check byte over all of it; any receiver that follows the 2009 framing stops before the trailer, and the 548-byte cap (NET-10) still holds. The server moves a link only for a datagram with its secret (compared in constant time); none or a wrong one: no move, counted and logged (the first 5, then every 1000th). The secret travels in clear: it stops anyone who cannot read the player's traffic (a carrier NAT, a campus, a shared network with client isolation), not someone on the path. | 64 bits; shell id 0xf3; trailer mark 0xd3 | close the NET-23 hijack and kick (review 2026-11-03) without breaking 2009 clients | none (`dc_wire::linkmove`) | `nat_rebind::a_stranger_behind_the_same_ip_cannot_take_or_close_a_silent_link`, `nat_rebind::two_clients_behind_one_ip_rebinding_at_once_each_keep_their_own_link`, `nat_rebind::a_client_without_the_secret_works_but_never_moves`, `nat_rebind::datagrams_with_the_trailer_stay_within_the_cap`, `linkmove::tests` |
| NET-25 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-25 proposed; project decision) | **A move never closes a link, and is rare.** A transport bye (`CTL_BYE` / `CTL_BYE_CODE`) closes a link only once the link has been on its address for 1000 ms: the datagram that moves a link and the ones right after it never close it (a client that leaves right then still ends its session with `C2S_BYE`, or by the silence drop). A link moves at most 3 times a minute. After a move every unacknowledged reliable block goes to the new address at once and an ack is due (what went to the old address is lost in the NAT), instead of after its resend timeout. | 1000 ms; 3 moves / 60 s | as stated | none (`BYE_AFTER_MOVE_MS`, `MOVE_LIMIT`, `MOVE_WINDOW_MS`) | `nat_rebind::a_bye_in_the_moving_datagram_does_not_close_the_link`, `nat_rebind::a_link_moves_at_most_three_times_a_minute`, `nat_rebind::queued_reliable_data_goes_to_the_new_address_at_once`, `nat_rebind::an_unreliable_only_datagram_with_the_secret_moves_the_link` |
| NET-26 (DC-DEFAULT: NET-26 proposed; project decision; amends UDP_TRANSPORT_2009.md §6.3) | **Liveness from good datagrams only.** The 2009 receiver stamps a link's last-receive time and traffic stamp before it tests the check byte, so junk sent to a link's address kept it alive (no idle drop, no DSV-490 silent drop, no NET-23 silence). Ours stamps both only for a datagram with a good check byte; a corrupt one is still dropped silently. Both sides. | none | as stated | none | `link::tests::corrupt_datagram_is_dropped_and_is_no_liveness`, `nat_rebind::junk_to_a_silent_link_does_not_keep_it_alive` |

Refused with a reason: `none` (the browser hid the attestation), self attestation, `fido-u2f` (no PIN), platform formats (`tpm`, `android-*`, `apple`), any other root, a synced passkey (backup-eligible flag). Both ceremonies check the client data (type, challenge, origin, not cross-origin), the rpId hash, user presence and user verification. ## Deploys from the admin dashboard (branch ops-deploy, USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 "It would also be good if I can trigger deploy commands from here when there's new updates available."; proposed, project decision; docs/DEPLOY_FROM_ADMIN.md)

| LG-392 (DC-DEFAULT: LG-392 proposed; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03) | **Deploy state and the request.** `[deploy] dir` (empty by default: no Updates content, no host builds) names the folder `tools/vps/deploy_setup.sh` makes (`/opt/decombat/deploy`, root:decombat 0750). Root writes and the lobby only reads: `available.json` (the fetch timer every 5 min: master, the running build of `bin/COMMIT.txt`, at most 50 commits since it with short sha, subject and author date, the 10 before and including it), `status.json` (id, sha, subject, targets, phase `fetching` / `building` / `packaging` / `waiting` / `installing` / `publishing` / `done` / `failed`, ok, message, started, updated, finished, the last 40 log lines), `history.jsonl` (the last 50 outcomes; the tab shows 10), `host/desired.txt` with the tarball. Each file over 1 MiB is not read. The lobby writes only `requests/<unix>-<8 hex>.json` (`sha`, `targets`, `end_matches`, `by`, `at`; one write of a new file; folder owned by `decombat`, the lobby unit's drop-in `ReadWritePaths=-<dir>/requests`). A deploy whose status has not moved for 3 h counts as dead. Root (`deploy_from_git.sh run`, started by `decombat-deploy.path`): one at a time (flock), the newest well-named regular file wins, every other entry is deleted unread, a request over 4096 bytes or of another shape is refused; `sha` must resolve in the mirror to one commit that is an ancestor of `refs/heads/<branch>`; `git archive` of it, the two builds of deploy_all.sh with `DC_GIT_COMMIT=<8 hex>` at nice 10, `tools/package_servers.sh` of that commit, then for `vps` (after waiting up to `MATCH_WAIT_MIN` = 15 min for `dc-dserver` processes to end unless `end_matches`) the tarball's own `deploy_remote.sh install` (install.sh; config and DB untouched; every enabled lobby restarted and checked), for `hosts` the tarball and `desired.txt` (`commit`, `tarball`, `sha256`, `size`) into `host/`, keeping the two newest tarballs. ## Account changes from the dashboard's Players tab (branch ops-player-admin, USER REQUEST 2026-11-03 "In the player tab can we add features such as giving NX, giving temporary or permanent bans, deleting account, etc?"; proposed, project decision; docs/OPS.md section 16)

| LG-395 (DC-DEFAULT: LG-395 proposed; USER REQUEST 2026-11-03) | **Giving and taking NX, GP, EXP.** `POST /ops/player/grant` `{"account", "nx", "gp", "exp", "reason"}`: signed whole numbers, at least one not 0, a reason required (at most 200 characters). Each at most its cap in one change (400); a change that would take a balance below 0 is refused (409), nothing is floored. NX is the prepaid balance (`characters.nx`, the one the NX rewards LG-310..LG-312 pay into and the shop's prepaid purchases spend). An online player's lobby sessions get 0x345 (NX) and 0x3004 with the popup flag 0 (GP / EXP), the pushes the lobby already sends after a match; 0x344 (the balance request the 2009 client sends after login and from its money panel) reads the DB, so it answers the new amount too. | LG-399 (DC-DEFAULT: LG-399 proposed; owner request 2026-11-03) | **Instances and the forwarding.** `[admin_web] instances` (at most 8; each `name` 1..32 of `a-z 0-9 -` and unique, `label` 1..40 characters, `admin` a loopback `ADDR:PORT` other than `admin_web.bind`, optional `env_file`) and `admin_web.label` (1..40, default "This lobby") are checked by `dc-config check`. The admin web serves `/i/<name>/ops` and `/i/<name>/ops/*` of a configured name only (another name: 404; `/i/<name>` redirects to `/i/<name>/ops`), after its own checks (LG-385 session: a page without one goes to `/login`, anything else 401; LG-387 Origin, JSON and the session's CSRF token, `X-Beta-CSRF` for `/ops/beta*`). The forwarder connects to `admin` (3 s) and sends `Host: <admin>`, the instance's admin token (`DC_ADMIN_TOKEN` of `env_file`, read at each request; `export` and quotes allowed) and, on a POST, `Origin: http://<admin>` and the instance's page token in `X-Admin-CSRF` and `X-Beta-CSRF`, read from its `GET /ops` page (`<meta name="csrf">`) just before; the body as received (at most 64 KiB, LG-382). The answer within 20 s (else 504), at most 8 MiB, must be JSON or HTML with a final status (1xx / 3xx: 502, never followed); a closed port is 502. Only the instance's `/ops` and `/ops/beta` pages may be HTML (else 502). Each forwarded POST is an `admin_web` event on the default lobby (`key #<n> from <address>: POST <path> on instance <name> (answer <status>)`). | as stated | one sign-in for every lobby of the box; the instance's loopback guard stays as it is and the browser never holds its token | `admin_web.label`, `admin_web.instances` | `adminfwd::{split, forwardable, inner_target, forward, parse_answer, token_from_env_file}`, `adminweb::instance`, `dc_config::check`; tests `adminweb::tests::a_further_instance_is_served_under_its_prefix_behind_the_same_session`, `adminfwd::tests::*`, dc-config `admin_web_instances_are_parsed_and_checked` |

| DSV-560 (DC-DEFAULT: DSV-560 proposed; project decision; amends DSV-460, DSV-500) | **Locked player doors.** A sliding or rotating door the world file marks player-activated AND locked is a use door that starts locked (the file's lock is its lock at the start): it is created in every room, co-op included, closed, with its activate entry disabled (no use prompt) while locked; `msg <door> unlock` / `lock` from any command text or trigger changes the lock and the entry follows (DSV-340 notes). The use key of a living player takes the nearest use door in reach (DSV-270) whatever its lock: a locked one does not turn, plays the file's locked sound at the door and runs its locked command, at most once per 500 ms per door (a burst of use packets queues one command and one sound). | 500 ms | SANDHOG_CP1's ten locked gates were message doors (DSV-500) and a co-op room left them out: an open doorway where the file has a shut gate; its one locked sliding door was unlocked for the use key (only the entry was disabled), so E opened it with no prompt. The file's locked command of four gates fires the trigger that unlocks the other side's gates; the file's trigger boxes in front of the others unlock them (DSV-563) | none | OBSERVED: ROM SANDHOG_CP1 (the eleven locked player doors, their locked sounds / commands, the unlocking triggers); survey of the 21 worlds: no other world has a locked door. The use key turns a switch at most once per 500 ms. Nested texts are followed for 32 rounds and at most 1024 statements per run: past the budget the run stops and drops what is pending (logged once per room), so triggers that fire themselves or each other twice cannot grow without end. A touched box fires itself (by its place in the list, not by name). The 0 / 1 value of `visible` / `solid` reads a number by its value (`0`, `0.0` false), the words `true` / `false` by their meaning, anything else as true when it has a byte other than `0`; the start scripts (DSV-37) read it the same way (the ROM worlds write only `0` and `1`). ## Bots fight on Gray Hammer, snipers scope, no shots at the dead (branch fix-bot-combat, owner report 2026-11-03 "Gray Hammer: the bots never fire", "bots shoot but rarely kill")

| BOT-112 (DC-DEFAULT: BOT-112 proposed; project decision; amends BOT-93 and BOT-111) | **The grid finds stairs, narrow ways and one-way drops.** A lattice step that is no flat step (or drop of at most 96) is tried as a stairway: sub-steps of 8 units, each a standing place at most 30 above the last (no drop) that the body raised by 30 reaches, 30..60 up in all; a stairway down is a lower place that climbs back up to the node. A standing place is searched from 30 above, else from the height itself, else 15 below (a way under a low ceiling). Where the lattice place is no way, the places half a step to either side are tried (doors and gaps the lattice columns miss). A link is walked back only when the way back climbs at most 30 or is a stairway (a ledge is no way up). A pulled straight leg takes no place more than 30 above the one 24 units before it. The plan's goal node is the nearest node within 144 units that sees the goal (a ray), else the nearest node. The grid is grown for the body's own box (the server's teleport box, at least BOT-1's), half the probes of a tick around the bot and half toward the goal. | 8 / 30..60 / 15 / 24 / 144 units | Gray Hammer TDM, 4 bots, 4 min: no bot ever saw an enemy (0 shots): from the north spawn the grid never reached the south half (steep stairs under a bridge, lattice-missed passages), the A* used drop links upward, and two bots stood on the two sides of one wall, each walking to the other's position; with BOT-112..117 the same run: 511 shots, 162 hit claims, 21 kills | none | `nav::tests::{a_stairway_steeper_than_the_lattice_step_is_climbed, a_drop_is_walked_down_only, a_plan_that_ends_behind_a_wall_from_the_goal_hands_over_to_the_greedy_finder}` |

## Default weapons and the backpack across entries (branch loadout-default-backpack, USER REPORT 2026-11-04)

| LG-403 (DC-DEFAULT proposed; USER DECISION 2026-11-04; amends CD-52, CD-77, LG-314) | **A default weapon never leaves its slot empty and is never stuck in the backpack.** (1) Stored loadout (CD-52 repair, every read and change): an empty weapon slot 0..3 takes the account's default weapon of that slot (default kind 1..4) from storage as before, or now also from a backpack slot 10..13, which it leaves. (2) View of an entry without the pack (LG-314): a hidden pack gun's slot shows the default of that slot from storage, else from a backpack slot, which then shows empty (0x323, 0x321 in-use word and the match's `loadout=` alike); the stored rows stay. (3) 0x324 into a backpack slot of a default weapon that holds its own slot as the entry shows it is refused (0x325 ok 0): another gun goes into that slot first. (4) 0x326 of a default weapon in a backpack slot as the entry shows it is accepted: it leaves the backpack, back to its own slot when that is empty, else to storage (the X of the backpack row, CLI-1160, and Equip on the cell, CLI-547, send it). Other defaults stay never unequipped (CD-77). A form or word not listed is skipped and counted. The DSV-562 budget (32 rounds, 1024 statements per run) covers nested bodies; at most 1024 bodies wait at once (was 256). | CLI-1865 (DC-DEFAULT: CLI-1865 proposed; USER REQUEST 2026-11-04) | **The swap (Windows).** The game folder is the exe's folder; it must take a test file, else the update falls back to the page. The zip (stored or deflated entries, every name checked as for mods, every CRC, at most 1 GB unpacked) goes to `dc-update/new`, the one top folder taken off; it must hold `dc-client.exe`. A copy of the running exe is started as `dc-update/helper.exe --finish-update <staging> <install> <pid> --relaunch <the run's arguments>` and the client quits as by its quit question. The helper takes only `<install>/dc-update/new`, waits up to 120 s for the process to end (`tasklist` on Windows, `kill -0` elsewhere), then moves each staged file to the same place; a replaced file goes to `dc-update/old` and every one comes back if a later file fails. Never replaced: `DeCombat.bat`, `bots.bat`, `known_servers.txt`, `launcher-name.txt`, `settings*`, `*.toml`, `*.ini`, `*.cfg`, `*.log`, `*.out`, `*.jsonl` (a differing new one is written beside as `<name>.new`), and nothing inside a folder that holds `Engine.exe`; nothing is deleted. The helper writes `dc-update/result.txt` (`ok` / `failed: <why>`) and starts the exe again with the same arguments. The next normal start removes `dc-update/` and shows a failure once. |
